gas_tank_water_heater.title: Gas water heater
gas_tank_water_heater.typical: a typical gas tank water heater

heat.say: The burner lights under the tank. Heat rises through the flue in the middle and warms the water around it.

lessons.label: The anode rod
lessons.say: The anode rod is a sacrificial metal rod. Over the years it slowly gets eaten away so your tank does not rust.

lessons.label: Sediment
lessons.say: Minerals in the water settle at the bottom of the tank as sediment. Too much makes the heater rumble and work harder.

electric_tank_water_heater.typical: a typical electric tank water heater

lessons.label: Sediment

heat.say: The thermostat calls for heat. A small fan clears the burner box, the igniter glows and the burners light. The flames heat the metal heat exchanger, and the big blower pushes your home's air across it and out the vents, warm. The fire and the air you breathe never touch.

lessons.label: Air conditioning
lessons.say: In summer the same blower pushes air through the cold coil on top. The coil pulls heat and moisture out of the air, and the water drips into a pan and drains away.

lessons.label: The filter
lessons.say: The filter catches dust before it reaches the blower and the coil. A clogged filter starves the system of air, so it runs longer and wears out sooner. Check it every month or two.

lessons.label: Heat exchanger
lessons.say: The heat exchanger keeps the flames and their exhaust apart from the air you breathe. Your technician checks it for cracks, because a crack could let exhaust into the airflow.

ac_condenser.title: Air conditioner outdoor unit
ac_condenser.typical: a typical air conditioner outdoor unit

heat.say: Inside your home, the refrigerant soaks up heat from the air. It is pumped out here, where the compressor squeezes it so it gets hotter than the outdoor air. The big fan pulls air in through the coil on the sides and blows that heat out the top. Then the refrigerant goes back inside to pick up more.

lessons.label: Keep the coil clear
lessons.say: The coil wraps around the sides of the unit, and air has to pass through it freely. Keep plants, grass clippings and leaves about two feet away. A dirty or blocked coil makes the unit work harder and cool less.

lessons.label: The power disconnect
lessons.say: The box on the wall near the unit is the power disconnect. Pulling out the block inside cuts the power to the outdoor unit, so it can be worked on safely. Technicians use it before they open the panel.

lessons.label: The capacitor
lessons.say: The capacitor gives the compressor and the fan motor a strong push to get started. It is one of the parts that wears out most often, especially after hot summers. If the fan will not spin or the unit just hums, it is one of the first things a technician checks. It holds a charge, so it is a job for a technician.

base_pan: The metal floor of the unit. The compressor and coil sit on it.
cabinet_posts: The corner posts that hold the unit's sides and top together.
louver_front: The slotted side panels. They protect the coil and let air pass through.
control_panel_cover: Covers the electrical parts in the corner. Only a technician should open it.
data_plate: Data label
Lists the model, size and age of the unit.
compressor: The heart of the system. It pumps the refrigerant around and squeezes it so it can give off its heat outdoors.
condenser_coil: Rows of thin metal fins around copper tubing. The heat from your home leaves through here. Keep it clean and clear.
fan: Pulls outdoor air through the coil and blows the heat out the top.
fan_motor: Turns the fan. If the fan stops, the unit cannot get rid of its heat.
fan_grille: The grille on top that keeps hands and debris out of the fan.
top_cap: The top of the cabinet. The fan and its guard sit in it.
orifice_ring: The ring around the fan that helps it pull air through the coil.
capacitor: Gives the compressor and fan motor a strong push to start. A common part to wear out. It holds a charge, so leave it to a technician.
contactor: A switch the thermostat controls. It turns the compressor and fan on and off.
control_box: Holds the electrical parts that start and run the unit.
service_valves: Where the copper lines from the house connect. Technicians check the refrigerant here.

whip: The flexible conduit that brings power from the disconnect to the unit.
pad: The flat base the unit sits on. It keeps the unit level and up off the ground.
heat_stream: The heat taken out of your home leaves here, blown up and away by the fan. Keep a few feet clear above the unit.

heat.say: The blower pulls your home's air in through the filter and across the cooling coil, then pushes it out into the ducts. In summer the coil is cold, so the air leaves cooler and drier. This one lies on its side, a common way to fit an air handler in an attic.

lessons.label: Electric heat
lessons.say: For heat, wire coils at the air outlet glow hot, a lot like a toaster, and the blower pushes your air across them. With a heat pump they help out on the coldest days. They work well but cost more to run than a heat pump.

lessons.label: The filter
lessons.say: The filter catches dust before it reaches the blower and the coil. Slide it out the way it went in, and match the arrow on the new one to the airflow. Check it every month or two.

lessons.label: Clogged filter
lessons.say: When the filter clogs, the blower cannot pull enough air across the cooling coil. The coil gets so cold that it can ice over, and the house stops cooling. Turn the system off, let the ice melt, and put in a clean filter. If it keeps freezing, call us.

lessons.label: Cooling coil
lessons.say: The coil gets cold when the air conditioning runs and pulls heat and moisture out of the air. The water drips into a pan under it and leaves through a drain line. Keeping the filter clean keeps the coil clean too.

filter: Catches dust before it reaches the blower and coil. Check it every month or two.

rails: Hold the unit up off the attic floor.

electric_tankless_water_heater.title: Electric tankless water heater
electric_tankless_water_heater.typical: a typical electric tankless water heater

front_marker.say: the front cover with its display

heat.say: Open a hot tap and a flow sensor feels the water moving. The control board turns on the heating elements, and the water warms as it passes through the heating chambers. It heats only while water flows, so there is no tank to keep hot.

lessons.label: Hard water
lessons.say: In hard water, minerals can coat the inside of the heating chambers. Scale makes the elements run hotter and wear out sooner. Where the water is hard, a technician can flush the heater through its service ports.

lessons.label: The inlet screen
lessons.say: A small screen catches grit where cold water comes in. If your hot water flow drops off, a clogged screen is a common cause. It is a quick rinse.

lessons.label: The power it needs
lessons.say: Heating water the moment you need it takes a lot of electricity. A whole house electric tankless heater often needs heavy wires and two or more large breakers, so your electrical panel has to have room for it.

status_led: Lights up while the heater is heating.

gas_tankless_water_heater.title: Gas tankless water heater
gas_tankless_water_heater.typical: a typical gas tankless water heater

front_marker.say: the front cover with its display

heat.say: Open a hot tap and water starts flowing through the heater. A fan mixes gas with air and the burner lights. The flame heats coiled tubes with your water running through them, so it comes out hot. There is no tank: it heats only while you use it.

lessons.label: Scale and flushing
lessons.say: Hard water leaves a mineral crust inside the heat exchanger, like the crust in a kettle. Scale slows the heat and can make the heater shut down with an error. A yearly flush through the service valves washes it out.

lessons.label: The condensate drain
lessons.say: This heater uses a second heat exchanger to pull extra heat out of its exhaust. That cools the exhaust so much that water forms, a little like dew. A trap and a drain line carry the water away, so keep that line clear.

lessons.label: Recirculation
lessons.say: Some homes add a small pump that keeps hot water moving through the pipes. Cooled water comes back to the heater on a return line and is heated again, so hot water reaches the far taps sooner. A timer runs it only when you need it.

lessons.label: The inlet screen
lessons.say: A small screen catches grit where cold water comes in. If your hot water flow drops off, a clogged screen is a common cause. It gets rinsed during a flush.

chassis: The metal case that holds the burner, heat exchangers and controls.

hybrid_water_heater.title: Hybrid water heater
hybrid_water_heater.typical: a typical hybrid heat pump water heater

heat.say: A fan pulls warm air from the room across a cold coil. A compressor, like the one in your refrigerator, moves that heat into the water in the tank. Cooler, drier air blows back out. Electric elements help out when you use a lot of hot water at once.

lessons.label: The air filter
lessons.say: The air filter keeps dust off the cold coil. A dirty filter makes the heat pump work harder and lean on the slower electric elements. Check it and rinse it every few months.

lessons.label: The anode rod
lessons.say: Like any steel tank, this one has a sacrificial anode rod. Over the years it slowly gets eaten away so your tank does not rust. Your technician can check it from the top.

lessons.label: The condensate drain
lessons.say: The cold coil pulls water out of the air, like a glass of ice water sweating on a summer day. That water runs out a drain line. Keep the line clear so it does not back up and spill.

outer_jacket: The metal skin around the tank. Insulation underneath keeps the hot water hot.
data_plate: Data label

air_filter: Keeps dust off the cold coil. Rinse it every few months.

tp_relief_valve: Opens by itself if the tank ever gets too hot or the pressure too high. An important safety part.
tp_discharge_connection: Carries water from the relief valve safely down toward the floor if it ever opens.
drain_valve: Used to flush sediment out of the bottom of the tank.
cold_supply_line: Where cold water from your home's supply comes in.
hot_supply_line: Where hot water leaves for your sinks, showers and appliances.
cold_shutoff_valve: Turns the water off to the heater for service.
hot_shutoff_valve: Closes the hot side for service.
expansion_tank: Gives the water room to grow as it heats, so pressure does not spike in the tank and pipes.
stand: Raises the heater off the floor.

heat.say: The indoor unit pulls room air in through the top, through the filters and across a cold coil. A long fan wheel blows the cooled air back out the bottom, and the vane steers it. Copper lines carry the heat through the wall to the outdoor unit, which blows it outside. Most can also run in reverse to heat in winter.

lessons.label: The filters
lessons.say: Lift the front panel and two mesh filters slide out. Rinse them in the sink and let them dry before they go back. Many makers suggest every few weeks when it runs a lot. Clogged filters cut the airflow and make the unit work harder.

lessons.label: The blower wheel
lessons.say: The long fan wheel and the coil sit in cool, damp air, so dust and mold can build up on them. That can cause a musty smell and weaker airflow. A technician can take the unit apart and deep clean them.

lessons.label: The drain
lessons.say: The coil pulls water out of the air. It drips into a tray and runs out through a drain line that goes through the wall with the copper lines. If that line clogs or does not slope downhill, water can drip from the unit and stain the wall.

front_panel: Lifts up so you can reach the filters.
chassis: The body of the indoor unit. The coil, fan and controls are inside.
intake_grille: Room air comes in through the top here.
filter_left: Two mesh screens that catch dust. Slide them out and rinse them every few weeks when it runs a lot.
coil: Gets cold when cooling, and hot when heating. Your room air passes through it.
blower_wheel: A long fan wheel that blows the air back into the room. Dust and mold on it cut the airflow.

vane: Swings up and down to steer the air into the room.
louvres: Steer the air left and right.

board: The unit's brain. It reads the remote and runs the fan and the outdoor unit.

back_plate: A metal plate on the wall that the indoor unit hangs on.
air_packets: Room air on its way back out, cooled or warmed.

garbage_disposal.title: Garbage disposal
garbage_disposal.typical: a typical garbage disposal under a kitchen sink

heat.say: Food drops onto a spinning plate at the bottom of the grind chamber. The plate flings it against a rough ring around the edge, which shreds it into tiny bits. Water carries the bits out the side and down the drain. There are no blades inside.

lessons.label: Run cold water
lessons.say: Run cold water before, during and for a few seconds after grinding. The water carries the bits all the way down the drain. Cold water keeps any grease firm so it gets chopped up instead of coating the pipes.

lessons.label: What to keep out
lessons.say: Keep grease, oil, bones, corn husks, celery strings, onion skins, coffee grounds, eggshells, pasta and rice out of the disposal. They tangle, swell or settle and can clog the drain. Small soft scraps with plenty of water are what it is made for.

lessons.label: If it hums or stops
lessons.say: If it hums but does not spin, switch it off first. A hex key in the socket on the bottom turns the motor by hand to free a jam. If it shut itself off, wait a few minutes and press the red reset button on the bottom. Never reach inside.

lessons.label: Dishwasher drain
lessons.say: The dishwasher often drains into the side of the disposal. Its hose loops up high under the counter so dirty sink water cannot run back into the dishwasher. When a new disposal goes in, a small plug inside that inlet has to be knocked out first, or the dishwasher cannot drain.

disposal_body: The motor and grind chamber in one housing, hanging under the sink drain.
disposal_mount: The ring in the sink's drain hole and the mount under it that holds the disposal up. A slow drip here usually means the seal under the sink flange needs redoing.
mount_lower_ring: Twists to lock the disposal onto the mount. Turning it the other way lets the disposal come down.
splash_guard: The rubber flaps in the sink opening. They keep food and spoons from flying out and are easy to replace when torn.
grind_chamber: Where the food is ground. The rough ring around the edge does the shredding.
turntable: Spins fast and throws food against the grind ring. The small lugs on it swing freely. They are not blades.
motor: The electric motor under the grind chamber that spins the plate.
shaft_seal: Keeps water out of the motor. When it wears out, the disposal can leak from the bottom, which usually means it is time for a new one.
reset_button: The red button on the bottom. The motor shuts itself off if it overheats or jams. Wait a few minutes, then press it.
jam_hex: A socket in the middle of the bottom. With the power off, a hex key here turns the motor by hand to free a jam.
discharge_elbow: Where the ground food and water leave the disposal, through a bent pipe into the drain.
disposal_cord: Plugs into the outlet under the sink. Many homes switch that outlet with a wall switch by the sink.
receptacle: The disposal plugs in here. It is often controlled by a wall switch.
dw_hose: Carries the dishwasher's drain water into the disposal. The high loop under the counter keeps sink water out of the dishwasher.
dw_supply: A braided hose that brings hot water to the dishwasher from the shutoff under the sink.
waste_arm: Carries water from the disposal over to the main drain.
waste_tee: Where the disposal's drain and the other sink bowl's drain join together.
p_trap: The curved pipe under the sink. It holds a little water that blocks sewer gas, and catches things before they go down the wall. Its slip nuts loosen so it can come off to clear a clog.
trap_water: The water that always sits in the trap. It is a seal that stops sewer gas from coming up the drain.
strainer_basket: The basket in the other sink bowl. It catches scraps and plugs the drain.
strainer_right: The drain fitting in the other sink bowl, sealed to the sink with gaskets and a big nut underneath.
tailpiece_right: The short straight pipe under the strainer that drops down to the drain tee.
stop_hot: Turns the hot water off to the faucet and, here, the dishwasher too.
stop_cold: Turns the cold water off to the faucet. Good to know where it is before you ever need it.
supply_hot: The flexible hose from the hot shutoff up to the faucet.
supply_cold: The flexible hose from the cold shutoff up to the faucet.
sink: A double bowl sink. The disposal hangs under one bowl.
faucet_pulldown: A pull down kitchen faucet. Run its cold water whenever the disposal is on.
cabinet: The cabinet under the sink. A quick look inside now and then catches small leaks early.
dishwasher: Its drain hose usually connects to the disposal or to the sink drain.

heat.say: Push the handle and the chain lifts the flapper at the bottom of the tank. The tank's water rushes down into the bowl, and the bowl empties through the curved trap like a siphon. The flapper drops shut, and the fill valve refills the tank until the float reaches the set line.

lessons.label: Running toilet
lessons.say: If the flapper no longer seals, tank water slowly slips into the bowl. The level drops until the fill valve turns on by itself to top it up, which is the hiss you may hear at night. A worn flapper is the usual cause and an easy part to replace. A few drops of food coloring in the tank tell you: color in the bowl without a flush means a leak.

lessons.label: Weak flush
lessons.say: If the chain has too much slack, the handle cannot lift the flapper all the way. It drops shut early and the bowl gets only part of the tank. A chain with just a little slack fixes it. A tank water level set too low gives a weak flush too.

lessons.label: Fill valve and float
lessons.say: After a flush the fill valve opens and refills the tank. The float rides up with the water and shuts the valve at the set line. The small refill tube tops up the bowl at the same time, through the overflow tube.

lessons.label: The shutoff
lessons.say: The small valve on the wall behind the toilet turns its water off. Turn it off before working in the tank, or if the bowl is about to overflow. An old or kinked supply line is worth replacing before it leaks.

bowl: The china bowl. A curved trap is molded inside it, out of sight, and carries everything to the drain in the floor.
bowl_water: The water that sits in the bowl seals the drain so sewer gas cannot come up into the room.
trap_flow: The curved channel inside the bowl. During a flush water fills it and pulls the bowl empty, like a siphon.
seat: Bolted to the bowl through two holes at the back.
seat_lid: The cover over the seat and bowl, hinged with the seat.
seat_hinges: Hold the seat and lid on. If the seat shifts side to side, the nuts under the bowl need a snug turn.
tank_shell: Holds the water for the next flush, usually about 1.3 to 1.6 gallons in newer toilets.
tank_lid: Heavy china that cracks if dropped. Set it down on a towel when you take it off.
tank_water: Clean water from your supply line, the same water as your sink. It waits here for the next flush.
handle: Turns the trip lever inside the tank.
trip_lever: The arm inside the tank that lifts the chain when you push the handle.
chain: Connects the trip lever to the flapper. It needs just a little slack: too tight and the flapper leaks, too loose and the flush is weak.
flapper: The rubber seal at the bottom of the tank. It lifts to flush and drops to seal. It wears out over the years and is the most common cause of a running toilet.
flush_valve: The opening the flapper seals, with a tall tube beside it. If the tank ever overfills, water spills down the tube into the bowl instead of onto the floor.
fill_valve: Refills the tank after every flush and shuts off when the float reaches the set line.
refill_tube: A small tube that tops up the bowl water during the refill, through the overflow tube.
float_cup: Rides up with the water and tells the fill valve when to stop. Raising or lowering it sets the tank's water level.
tank_bolts: Hold the tank to the bowl, each with a rubber washer to keep water in.
spud_gasket: The big rubber seal between the tank and the bowl. An old one can leak where the two meet.
angle_stop: Turns the water off to the toilet. Good to know where it is before you ever need it.
supply_line: The short hose that carries water from the shutoff up to the fill valve.
wax_ring: Seals the toilet to the drain in the floor. A toilet that rocks can break this seal, so water or odor may show at the base.
flange: The ring on the drain pipe in the floor. The toilet bolts down to it.
bolt_caps: Two bolts hold the toilet to the flange, hidden under small caps at the base.

water_softener.title: Water softener
water_softener.typical: a typical two tank water softener

heat.say: Hard water comes in at the valve on top and flows down through a bed of tiny resin beads. The beads grab the hardness minerals, calcium and magnesium, and trade them for a little sodium. Soft water rises up the center tube and goes on to your home.

lessons.label: Regeneration
lessons.say: After enough gallons the beads are full and need a wash, usually in the middle of the night. The valve runs water backward through the tank, draws salty brine from the brine tank to clean the beads, rinses them and sends the waste water down the drain. Here you see the backwash step.

lessons.label: Salt bridge
lessons.say: Salt can form a hard crust with an empty space under it, called a salt bridge. The tank looks full, but no salt reaches the water, so the softener stops softening. Push a broom handle down through the salt to break it up, and keep the salt above half full.

lessons.label: The bypass
lessons.say: The bypass valve sends water around the softener, handy when it needs work. While it is on bypass your home gets hard water. If your water seems hard again, check that the bypass was not left turned.

lessons.label: The control
lessons.say: The control keeps the time of day and your water's hardness setting, and counts the gallons used. After a long power outage, check that the clock is right so regeneration still happens at night.

resin_tank: The tall tank. It is filled with tiny resin beads that pull hardness minerals out of the water as it passes through.
valve_head: The valve on top of the resin tank. It steers water through the tank, and runs the cleaning cycle when the beads are full.
control_cover: Shows the time and status. The time of day, your water's hardness and the cleaning time are set here.
control_board: The small circuit board under the cover. It keeps the clock and decides when to regenerate.
display_service: Shows the time of day when the softener is working normally, and the cycle step while it cleans itself.
meter_dome: Counts the gallons that go through, so the softener cleans itself after real use instead of on a fixed calendar.
bypass_valve: Sends water around the softener when it needs work. Left on bypass, your home gets hard water.
inlet_stub: Where water from your home's main line comes into the softener.
outlet_stub: Where softened water leaves for the rest of your home.
drain_line: A small tube that carries the rinse water from each cleaning cycle to a drain.
drain_stub: The drain line should end above the drain with a gap of air, so dirty water can never be pulled back into the softener.
brine_tank: The shorter tank. It holds the salt and the salty water, called brine, used to clean the resin beads.
brine_lid: Lift it to check the salt. A look about once a month is a good habit.
salt_bed: Softener salt slowly dissolves into the water below it to make brine. Keep it above half full and below the top.
salt_bridge: A hard crust of salt with an empty space under it. The tank looks full, but the softener cannot make brine. Break it up with a broom handle.
salt_grid: A platform a few inches up. The salt sits on it and the brine forms underneath.
brine_water: Salty water at the bottom of the tank. The valve draws it up to clean the resin beads.
brine_well: A slotted tube that keeps salt away from the float and the brine line.
brine_float: Shuts off the refill if anything goes wrong, so the brine tank cannot overflow.
brine_line: The small tube between the two tanks. Brine is drawn up through it, and fresh water goes back down it to refill.
wall_transformer: Plugs into a wall outlet and turns house power into low voltage for the control.
power_cord: Carries low voltage power from the adapter to the control.
receptacle: Where the softener's power adapter plugs in.

heat.say: Wastewater from the house flows into the air chamber. The air pump in the yard blows air down to the bottom, where it bubbles up and keeps the water mixing, so helpful bacteria can break the waste down. The water then passes under a wall into the settling side, where leftover bits sink, and the clear water leaves past the chlorine tablets to the spray or drip field.

lessons.label: Chlorine tablets
lessons.say: The water passes the chlorine tablets on its way out, which kills germs before it reaches the yard. Check the tablets about once a month and add more when they run low. Use only tablets made for septic chlorinators, never pool tablets.

lessons.label: Air pump filter
lessons.say: The air pump should run all day and night. It breathes through a small filter under the cover on top, and a dirty filter starves the tank of air. A filter like this one needs a rinse or a new one. Keep the pump plugged in, and call if it ever goes quiet.

lessons.label: The alarm
lessons.say: A float in the tank rises if the water gets too high, and that turns on the alarm light on the air pump. It usually means something needs service, like a clog or a pump problem. Cut back on water use and call for service. The tank can hold some extra water until help arrives.

lessons.label: Pumping
lessons.say: Over time, solids the bacteria cannot break down settle on the bottom, and a scum layer floats on top. A service technician checks these and has the tank pumped when they build up. Keeping wipes, grease and harsh cleaners out of the drains helps the bacteria and stretches the time between pumpings.

tank: A buried tank with two sides: an air chamber where bacteria break the waste down, and a settling side where the water clears.
water: Wastewater is mixed with air here all the time. The air feeds helpful bacteria that break the waste down.
water_clarifier: Calm water where leftover bits sink, so only clear water leaves the tank.
baffle: Separates the air chamber from the settling side. Water passes underneath it.
bubbles: Air from the pump rises through the water. It keeps the bacteria alive and the water mixing.
diffuser: A drilled pipe on the bottom of the air chamber. Air from the pump comes out of it as bubbles.
air_line: Carries air from the pump down to the diffuser at the bottom of the tank.
airlift: A small pipe that uses air to lift floating bits from the settling side back into the air chamber to be treated again.
float_switch: Floats on the water in the tank. If the water rises too high, it tips up and turns on the alarm.
float_cable: Connects the alarm float to the alarm on the air pump.
inlet: Where wastewater from the house enters the tank.
outlet: Where clear, treated water leaves the tank and heads to the chlorinator and the field.
chlorinator: A tube that holds chlorine tablets. Treated water flows past them and is cleaned of germs before it reaches the yard.
chlor_tablets: Slowly dissolve to kill germs. Check them about once a month, and use only tablets made for septic chlorinators.
chlorinator_cap: The cap at ground level. Lift it off to check and add tablets.
chlor_feed_tube: Holds the stack of tablets. Pull it up to see how many are left.
lid_aeration: Opens over the air chamber for service. Keep it screwed down so children and pets stay safe.
lid_clarifier: Opens over the settling side for service. Keep it screwed down, and never reach or climb into a tank.
riser_aeration: A tube that brings the tank opening up to the ground, so the tank can be checked and pumped without digging.
air_pump: Sits in the yard and pumps air into the tank all day and night. If it stops, the bacteria stop working, so keep it plugged in.
pump_cover: Keeps weather off the pump's working parts.
pump_internals: A small motor and rubber diaphragms that push air. They wear over the years and can be rebuilt or replaced.
pump_filter: Cleans the air the pump breathes in. Rinse or replace it when it looks dirty.
pump_filter_dirty: A clogged filter like this one chokes the pump, so the tank gets less air.
pump_filter_cover: Lifts off the top of the pump to reach the air filter.
alarm_lit: Comes on when the water in the tank is too high. Cut back on water use and call for service.
pump_pad: A small base that keeps the air pump level and up off the wet ground.
pump_hose: Connects the air pump to the buried air line.
air_line_ground: Carries air underground from the pump to the tank.
power_cord: Brings power to the air pump. The pump needs power all the time to keep the system working.
sludge_blanket: Solids the bacteria cannot break down settle here. A technician checks the depth and has the tank pumped when it builds up.
scum_layer: Grease and light bits floating on top. It is removed when the tank is pumped.
sewer_line: Carries everything from the house drains to the tank.
cleanout: A pipe up to the ground between the house and the tank. A plumber uses it to clear a clog in the sewer line.
cleanout_plug: The screw cap on top of the cleanout. Keep it on tight.

aerobic_septic_spray.title: Aerobic septic with spray field
aerobic_septic_spray.typical: a typical aerobic septic system with a spray field

heat.say: Wastewater from the house first settles in the trash chamber, where solids sink and grease floats. In the middle chamber, air from the air pump bubbles up through the water so helpful bacteria can break the waste down. The water settles again, passes the chlorine tablets and collects in the pump chamber. When it fills, a float turns on the pump, which sends the water out to sprinkler heads in the yard.

lessons.label: Chlorine tablets
lessons.say: On its way to the pump chamber, the water passes the chlorine tablets, which kill germs before it is sprayed in the yard. Check the tablets about once a month and add more when they run low. Use only tablets made for septic chlorinators, never pool tablets.

lessons.label: Air pump filter
lessons.say: The air pump should run all day and night. Without air, the bacteria stop working and the water leaving the tank is poorly treated and smelly. The pump breathes through a small filter under a cover, and a dirty one like this needs a rinse or a new one. Keep the pump plugged in, and call if it goes quiet.

lessons.label: Pump and float
lessons.say: As the pump chamber fills, the float rises and tips, and that turns the pump on. When the water drops, the float hangs back down and the pump shuts off. If the pump ever fails, the water keeps rising and the system's alarm lets you know. Cut back on water use and call for service.

lessons.label: Pumping
lessons.say: The trash chamber collects what the bacteria cannot break down, as sludge on the bottom and scum on top. A service technician checks these and has the tank pumped when they build up. Keeping wipes, grease and harsh cleaners out of the drains helps the bacteria and stretches the time between pumpings.

tank: A buried tank split into chambers: one to settle the trash out, one to treat with air, one to settle again, and one for the pump.
water_inlet: The first chamber. Solids sink and grease floats here, so they do not reach the air chamber.
water_aer: Air is bubbled through the water here all the time. It feeds helpful bacteria that break the waste down.
water_clar: Calm water where leftover bits sink, so only clearer water moves on.
water_pump: Holds the treated water until there is enough to spray. Then the pump sends it out to the yard.
scum_inlet: Grease and light bits floating in the trash chamber. They are removed when the tank is pumped.
sludge: Solids that settle on the bottom of the trash chamber. A technician checks the depth and has it pumped when it builds up.
inlet: Where wastewater from the house drops into the trash chamber.
inlet_boot: A rubber boot where the sewer pipe passes through the tank wall. It keeps ground water out and wastewater in.
inlet_stub: Carries everything from the house drains to the tank.
lid_inlet: Opens over the trash chamber for checking and pumping.
lid_aer: Opens over the air chamber for service.
lid_pump: Opens over the pump chamber, where the pump, float and chlorinator are reached.
riser_aer: A tube that brings a tank opening up to the ground, so the tank can be checked and pumped without digging.
bolts_aer: Hold each lid down so children and pets stay safe. Keep them in, and never reach or climb into a tank.
blower: Sits beside the tank and pumps air into it all day and night. If it stops, the bacteria stop working, so keep it plugged in.
blower_air_filter: Cleans the air the pump breathes in. Rinse or replace it when it looks dirty.
blower_air_filter_cover: Opens to reach the air pump's filter.
blower_air_filter_dirty: A clogged filter like this one chokes the pump, so the tank gets less air.
air_line: Carries air from the pump to the tank.
aeration_pipe: Carries air down to the bottom of the air chamber, where it comes out as bubbles.
bubbles: Air rising through the water. It keeps the bacteria alive and the water mixing.
blower_cord: Brings power to the air pump. The pump needs power all the time.
blower_receptacle: The weatherproof outlet on a post where the air pump plugs in.
surge_device: Plugs in at the outlet and helps protect the air pump from power surges and lightning.
transfer: Carries clear water from the settling chamber toward the pump chamber, past the chlorine tablets.
chlor_feed_tube: A tube that holds chlorine tablets. Pull it up from the lid to see how many are left.
chlor_tablets: Slowly dissolve to kill germs in the water before it is sprayed. Use only tablets made for septic chlorinators.
chlor_tee_drop: The fitting where water flows past the bottom of the tablets on its way to the pump chamber.
pump: Sits at the bottom of the pump chamber and pushes the treated water out to the sprinkler heads.
float_onoff: Rises with the water. When it tips up, the pump turns on, and when it hangs down, the pump shuts off.
discharge_upper: Carries water from the pump out of the tank to the spray line.
union_nut: A threaded joint in the pump pipe, so a technician can lift the pump out for service.
spray_line: A buried pipe that carries treated water from the pump out to the sprinkler heads.
spray_head0: Pops up and sprays treated water over the lawn, where grass and soil finish the job. Keep the heads clear of tall grass and do not drive over them.

bath_sink.title: Bathroom sink
bath_sink.typical: a typical bathroom sink and vanity

heat.say: Hot and cold come out of the wall through two small shutoff valves, then up flexible lines to the faucet. Each handle turns a cartridge that lets its water through. Used water runs down the drain, through the U shaped trap under the sink, and into the drain pipe in the wall.

lessons.label: The P trap
lessons.say: The U shaped bend under the sink always holds a little water. That water is a seal that keeps sewer gas out of the room. Rings, earrings and caps that go down the drain usually stop here, and the nuts on each end unscrew by hand so it can come off.

lessons.label: Pop up drain
lessons.say: The knob behind the faucet moves a rod under the sink, which tips a lever into the drain and moves the stopper. Pull the knob up to close the drain, push it down to open it. Hair and soap build up on the stopper over time and slow the sink. Lifting the stopper out and cleaning it often fixes a slow drain.

lessons.label: Shutoff valves
lessons.say: The two small valves on the wall under the sink turn off the hot and cold to this faucet only. Turn them off before working on the faucet, or if a supply line leaks. Valves that sit unused for years can stick or drip, so turning them now and then is worth it.

vanity_top: The top with the sink bowl molded in. The caulk where it meets the wall keeps splashes out of the cabinet.
cabinet: Holds up the top and hides the plumbing. A soft or stained cabinet floor often means a slow leak above it.
door_left: Open them to reach the trap, the drain linkage and the shutoff valves.
mirror: Hangs on the wall above the vanity.
bowl_water: Water from the faucet on its way down the drain.
faucet: Brings hot and cold together and pours from the spout. It is held to the top by nuts underneath.
handle_hot: Turns the hot cartridge on and off.
handle_cold: Turns the cold cartridge on and off.
cartridge_hot: Opens and closes the hot water inside the faucet. A drip from the spout usually means a worn cartridge, and it can be replaced on its own.
cartridge_cold: Opens and closes the cold water inside the faucet. A drip from the spout usually means a worn cartridge, and it can be replaced on its own.
bonnet_hot: Holds the cartridge down in the faucet body, under the handle.
aerator: The small screen at the tip of the spout. It mixes air into the stream. Hard water and grit clog it, so unscrewing and rinsing it often fixes weak flow.
faucet_tubes: Where the supply lines connect under the faucet.
mount_nut_hot: Hold the faucet tight to the countertop. A faucet that wobbles needs these snugged up.
stopper: Moves up to let water drain and down to hold it in the bowl. Hair and soap collect on it.
lift_rod: The knob behind the faucet. Pull it up to close the drain, push it down to open it.
clevis_strap: A metal strap with holes that joins the lift rod to the pivot rod. Moving the rod to another hole adjusts how far the stopper opens.
spring_clip: Holds the pivot rod in the clevis strap's hole.
pivot_rod: A rod that goes into the side of the drain and pushes the stopper up and down.
pivot_nut: Seals the spot where the pivot rod enters the drain. A drip here is common and a snug turn often stops it.
popup_drain: The drain fitting in the bottom of the bowl that the stopper sits in.
tailpiece: The straight pipe from the drain body down to the trap.
j_bend: The U shaped bend under the sink. It holds water that keeps sewer gas out, and it is where dropped rings usually stop.
trap_water: The water that always sits in the trap. If a sink is not used for months it can dry out and let sewer smell in; running the water refills it.
j_nut_in: Hand tight nuts with washers inside that seal each end of the trap. They let the trap come off without tools.
p_trap_arm: The pipe from the trap back to the drain in the wall.
wall_stub: Where the sink drain joins the house drain pipe.
drain_escutcheon: A trim ring that covers the hole where the drain pipe comes out of the wall.
stop_hot: Turns off hot water to this faucet only. Turn the handle clockwise to close it.
stop_cold: Turns off cold water to this faucet only. Turn the handle clockwise to close it.
supply_hot: The flexible hose from the shutoff valve up to the faucet. Many last years, but a bulging, kinked or rusty one is worth replacing before it leaks.
supply_cold: The flexible hose from the shutoff valve up to the faucet. Many last years, but a bulging, kinked or rusty one is worth replacing before it leaks.

heat.say: When your air conditioner or furnace runs, it makes water. The water runs down a hose into this small tank. As it rises, a float turns the pump on, and the pump pushes the water up the tube to a drain. A check valve keeps it from running back down.

lessons.label: Stuck float
lessons.say: Slime and algae can stick the float, so the pump never turns on. The water keeps rising. A second float can shut the cooling off before it spills, if it is wired in. If not, the tank overflows. A puddle or a water stain by the pump is a sign it needs a look.

lessons.label: Keeping it clean
lessons.say: Slime builds up in the tank over time. About once a year, with the pump unplugged, the lid lifts off so the tank and float can be rinsed clean. A clean tank keeps the float moving freely.

lessons.label: The drain tube
lessons.say: The tube carries the water away, often up a wall and across the ceiling. If it kinks or clogs, or the check valve sticks, the pump runs but the water cannot leave. A pump that runs a long time without the water dropping is worth a check.

reservoir: A small tank that collects the water from your cooling coil or furnace.
lid: Holds the motor, pump and floats. It lifts off for cleaning.
float: Rises with the water and turns the pump on, then drops and turns it off.
float_safety: Sits higher than the main float. If the water gets too high, it can shut the cooling off before the tank spills.
float_stuck: A float held down by slime or algae. The pump never starts and the water keeps rising.
impeller: A small spinning wheel that pushes the water up the tube.
motor_fan: Keeps the small motor cool while it runs.
check_valve: Lets water out to the tube and keeps it from running back into the tank.
discharge_tube: Carries the water away to a drain. Keep it free of kinks.
discharge_clamp: Holds the drain tube on the check valve.
tube_clips: Hold the drain tube against the wall along its run.
discharge_stub: Where the drain tube leaves the room for the drain.
inlet_hose: Brings the water from the cooling coil drain into the tank.
inlet_clamp: Holds the inlet hose on the drain fitting.
power_cord: Plugs into a nearby outlet. The pump needs power to work.
safety_leads: Connect the safety float to the cooling controls, so a full tank can turn the cooling off.
reservoir_water: Water from the coil, waiting for the float to rise.
water_rise: As the water rises, it lifts the float until the pump starts.
puddle: Water that spilled out of a full tank.
flow_packets: Water pushed up the tube to the drain.

erv.title: Fresh air exchanger (ERV)
erv.typical: a typical fresh air exchanger, also called an ERV

heat.say: One fan pulls stale air out of your home and sends it outside. A second fan brings the same amount of fresh outdoor air in. Both streams pass through the core, where the outgoing air hands its heat or coolness and some moisture to the incoming air, without the two ever mixing. You get fresh air without throwing away much of what you paid to heat or cool.

lessons.label: Filters and core
lessons.say: Open the door and the core slides out. Filters on the core catch dust and pollen before they reach it. Many makers suggest checking the filters every few months and washing or replacing them. Follow the manual for cleaning the core itself.

lessons.label: Clogged filters
lessons.say: Dusty filters and a dirty core choke the airflow. The unit still runs but moves much less fresh air, and the house can feel stuffy. Clean filters bring it back.

lessons.label: Two fans
lessons.say: There are two fans, one for each stream of air. They move about the same amount, so the house is not pushed or pulled out of balance. If one stops, the unit can no longer trade air the right way.

cabinet: The insulated box that holds the core, the fans and the controls.
door: Opens so the filters and core can come out for cleaning.
core: Thin layers that let the outgoing air warm or cool the incoming air, and pass along some moisture, without the air mixing.
core_filters: Catch dust and pollen before the air reaches the core. Check them every few months.
core_clogged: Dust built up in the core. Air moves slowly through it.
filters_dirty: Filters full of dust. They choke the airflow until they are cleaned or replaced.
blower_supply_wheel: Brings fresh outdoor air in and sends it to your home.
blower_exhaust_wheel: Pulls stale air from your home and sends it outside.
blower_housings: The shells around the two fans that guide the air.
electrical_drawer: Holds the unit's controls and wiring. Leave it to a technician.
terminal_block: Where the control wires connect to the unit.
control_button: A button on the unit, often used to switch it on or reset it.
control_led: Shows the unit has power. Some blink a code when something needs attention.
port_fresh_in: The collar where fresh outdoor air enters the unit.
port_exhaust_out: The collar where stale air leaves the unit on its way outside.
port_stale_in: The collar where stale air from your home enters the unit.
port_supply_out: The collar where fresh air leaves the unit on its way into your home.
duct_fresh_in: Brings outdoor air from the hood on the wall to the unit.
duct_exhaust_out: Carries stale air from the unit up and out through the roof.
duct_stale_in: Brings stale air from a grille in the house to the unit.
duct_supply_out: Carries fresh air from the unit to your home's duct system.
supply_takeoff: Where the fresh air joins your home's ducts, so it is spread to the rooms.
grille_stale: A grille in the ceiling where stale air is pulled out of the house. Keep it dusted.
hood_intake: Where outdoor air comes in. Keep it clear of leaves, nests and lint.
hood_exhaust: Where stale air leaves the house.
hangers: Hold the unit up from the framing above.
wall_control: Turns the unit on and sets how much it runs.
control_cable: Connects the wall control to the unit.
interlock_cable: A thin wire to the air handler, so the home's blower can run along with it and spread the fresh air.
power_cord: Plugs the unit into its outlet.
receptacle: The outlet the unit plugs into.
feed_cable: Brings power to the unit's outlet.
fresh_packet_00: Outdoor air on its way in, warmed or cooled by the core first.
stale_packet_00: Indoor air on its way out of the house.

heat_pump.title: Heat pump outdoor unit
heat_pump.typical: a typical heat pump outdoor unit

heat.say: A heat pump moves heat instead of making it. In summer it carries heat out of your home, and the fan blows it out the top. In winter a valve inside flips the flow, so the outdoor coil pulls heat from the outdoor air, even cold air, and sends it inside. The same compressor and fan do both jobs.

lessons.label: Defrost in winter
lessons.say: On cold, damp days frost builds up on the outdoor coil. Every so often the unit switches to defrost. The valve flips for a few minutes, the fan stops, and the coil warms up to melt the ice. You may hear a whoosh and see steam. That is normal. Ice that stays thick for hours is worth a call.

lessons.label: Keep the coil clear
lessons.say: Air has to pass freely through the coil on the sides, summer and winter. Keep plants, leaves and grass clippings about two feet away, and keep the top clear. A dirty or blocked coil makes the unit work harder and heat and cool less.

lessons.label: The capacitor
lessons.say: The capacitor gives the compressor and the fan motor a strong push to start. It is one of the parts that wears out most often, and a worn one can swell on top like this. If the fan will not spin or the unit just hums, it is one of the first things a technician checks. It holds a charge, so it is a job for a technician.

lessons.label: The compressor
lessons.say: With the sides off you can see the compressor, the pump that moves the refrigerant around. A padded jacket around it keeps it quieter. A small heater band keeps it warm in cold weather so it starts easily.

base_pan: The metal floor of the unit. The compressor and coil sit on it.
louver_front: The slotted side panels. They protect the coil and let air pass through.
control_panel_cover: Covers the electrical parts in the corner. Only a technician should open it.
service_pocket: The lower corner panel. The copper lines and wires come in behind it.
data_plate: Data label
Lists the model, size and age of the unit.
top_cap: The top of the cabinet. The fan and its guard sit in it.
fan_grille: The grille on top that keeps hands and debris out of the fan.
fan: Pulls outdoor air through the coil and blows it out the top.
fan_motor: Turns the fan. If the fan stops, the unit cannot trade heat with the outdoor air.
compressor: The heart of the system. It pumps the refrigerant around, for heating and for cooling.
sound_jacket: A padded blanket around the compressor that keeps it quieter.
crankcase_heater: A small heater band that keeps the compressor warm in cold weather so it starts easily.
compressor_terminal_cover: A cover over the spot where the power wires connect to the compressor.
condenser_coil: Rows of thin metal fins around copper tubing. It gives off heat in summer and gathers heat in winter. Keep it clean and clear.
reversing_valve: Flips the direction the refrigerant flows. That is what lets the same unit heat or cool your home.
accumulator: A tank that catches liquid refrigerant before it can reach the compressor. It protects the compressor, most of all when heating.
filter_drier: A small canister that catches moisture and grit in the refrigerant.
pressure_switches: Shut the unit off if the refrigerant pressure gets too high or too low.
refrigerant_lines: Copper tubing that carries the refrigerant between the compressor, the coil, the valve and the house.
service_valves: Where the copper lines from the house connect. Technicians check the refrigerant here.
capacitor: Gives the compressor and fan motor a strong push to start. A common part to wear out. It holds a charge, so leave it to a technician.
capacitor_bulged: A worn capacitor can swell on top. The unit may hum and not start. A technician replaces it.
contactor: A switch the thermostat controls. It turns the compressor and fan on and off.
defrost_board: A small circuit board that decides when the coil needs to defrost in winter, then runs the defrost.
control_box: Holds the electrical parts that start and run the unit.
control_wiring: Wires that connect the controls to the compressor, the fan and the valve.
coil_dirty: Dirt, grass and leaves packed into the fins. Air cannot get through, so the unit works harder.
disconnect: A box on the wall near the unit. Pulling out the block inside cuts the power to the unit for service.
disconnect_pullout: The removable block inside the disconnect. Out means the unit has no power.
whip: The flexible conduit that brings power from the disconnect to the unit.
lineset: Two copper lines run between this unit and the indoor unit. The bigger one wears foam insulation. Cracked or missing foam is worth replacing.
lineset_wall_plate: Covers the hole where the copper lines go through the wall.
thermostat_wire: A thin wire that carries the thermostat's signals to the unit.
pad: The flat base the unit sits on. It keeps the unit level and up off the ground.
heat_stream: Air blown out the top. It is warm when the unit is cooling your home and cool when it is heating it. Keep a few feet clear above the unit.

lift_station.title: Sewer lift station
lift_station.typical: a typical sewer lift station with a grinder pump

heat.say: Every drain in the house flows down to this basin. When the water lifts the middle float and tips it past its angle, the panel starts the grinder pump. It chops the waste fine and pushes it up a small pipe to the sewer. When the level drops and the bottom float tips back down, the pump stops.

lessons.label: The floats
lessons.say: Three floats hang on cords at different heights. Each one rises with the water and only clicks its switch once it tips past its angle. The bottom one stops the pump, the middle one starts it, and the red one at the top sets off the high water alarm.

lessons.label: If the alarm goes off
lessons.say: The red light on the panel means the water rose to the top float, so the pump is not keeping up. Stop using water: hold the laundry, dishwasher, showers and flushing. Many panels also sound a buzzer with a silence switch, but the light stays on. Then call for service. The basin has some room left, which is your time to get help.

lessons.label: What to keep out
lessons.say: A grinder handles normal toilet and kitchen waste. Grease, wipes (even the flushable kind), paper towels and feminine products build up on the water, wrap the cutter and foul the floats. Keeping them out of every drain is the best thing you can do for it.

lessons.label: The control panel
lessons.say: The panel runs the pump from the floats. The switch inside normally sits on AUTO. There is live power in the box, so leave the inside to a technician. Keep the door latched and the station's breaker and disconnect switched on.

basin: A buried fiberglass tank that collects everything that drains from the house until the pump sends it on.
riser: Extends the basin up to ground level so the cover sits at the surface.
lid: Bolted down so no one can lift it or fall in. Keep it clear and never drive over it.
lid_bolts: Stainless bolts that hold the cover on. All of them should always be in.
vent: Lets the basin breathe as the water rises and falls.
pump: Sits on the basin floor. A spinning cutter under it chops waste into a slurry so it can be pushed through a small pipe.
lift_chain: Used to raise the pump out of the basin for service, so no one pulls it by its cord.
chain_hook: Holds the top of the lift chain where it can be reached with the cover off.
discharge_riser: Carries the ground waste up from the pump. It comes out with the pump.
discharge_water: The check valve keeps this water held in the pipe between pump runs.
check_valve: Lets water go up and out, but stops what is in the outgoing pipe from draining back into the basin.
check_poppet: The spring loaded part inside the check valve that closes when the pump stops.
union_nut: A joint that unscrews by hand so the pump and its pipe can come out.
gate_valve: Closes the outgoing pipe so a technician can work on the pump or check valve.
gate_handwheel: Turns the shutoff valve. It should be left fully open.
discharge_run: Carries the pumped waste out through the basin wall.
force_main: The small pressure pipe that takes the waste from the station to the sewer line or main.
sewer_line: Drains from the house flow downhill through this pipe into the basin.
cleanout: A capped opening on the sewer line so a clog between the house and the basin can be cleared.
inflow: Water arriving from the house drains.
inlet_grommet: A rubber seal where the sewer pipe enters the basin.
water_fill: Rises as the house drains and falls each time the pump runs.
float_off: The lowest float. When the water drops and it tips back down, the pump stops.
float_on: The middle float. When the water lifts it past its angle, the pump starts.
float_alarm: The red float at the top. If the water reaches it, the alarm light on the panel comes on.
float_weights: Small weights on the cords that keep each float at its set height.
cords: Tied along the pipe and run to the panel through a conduit.
conduit: A pipe that protects the wires from the basin to the panel.
control_panel: Runs the pump from the floats and holds the alarm light. It is mounted where it can be seen.
panel_door: Keep it latched so rain stays out. Water inside the box is a common cause of panel trouble.
alarm_lit: Lit means high water. Stop using water and call for service.
hoa_switch: Normally on AUTO so the floats run the pump. HAND is for a technician running it by hand.
hoa_lever_auto: The normal setting: the floats decide when the pump runs.
disconnect: A shutoff near the station that cuts all power to it, for safe service.
motor_starter: Shuts the pump off if it draws too much power. A technician checks why before resetting it.

heat.say: Air coming back from your rooms passes through this cabinet on its way to the air handler. Inside, a thick pleated filter catches dust, pet hair and pollen. Because it is several inches deep, it has far more filter area than a thin filter, so it catches more and still lets the air through easily.

lessons.label: Changing the filter
lessons.say: Open the door and the filter slides out. Slide the new one in with its arrow pointing the way the air moves. Many deep filters last about six to twelve months, sooner with pets or dusty work in the house. The label on the filter or the cabinet says what size to buy.

lessons.label: A dirty filter
lessons.say: A filter packed with dust holds the air back. The system runs longer, less air comes out the vents, and in summer the cooling coil can even ice over. If the filter looks gray all over, it is time for a new one.

lessons.label: Room to reach it
lessons.say: The filter comes out through the door, so it needs open room beside the cabinet. If boxes or framing block the door, the filter cannot be changed and it tends to get forgotten. Keep that space clear.

ah_media_cabinet: The metal box that holds the deep filter between the return duct and the air handler.
ah_media_door: Opens so the filter can slide out. Keep room clear in front of it.
ah_media_filter: A thick pleated filter, several inches deep. It catches dust, pet hair and pollen and lasts much longer than a thin filter.
ah_media_filter_frame: Holds the pleats in shape and seals the filter against the cabinet.
media_loaded: A filter packed with dust. It holds the air back until it is replaced.
ah_media_transition: Connects the cabinet to the air handler. Clean air leaves through here.
ah_media_transition_in: The duct bringing air back from your rooms connects here.
ah_media_tape: Foil tape seals the joints so unfiltered air cannot sneak around the filter.
ah_media_test_port: A small plugged hole. A technician measures the air pressure on each side of the filter to see how much it is holding the air back.
ah_media_arrow: Shows which way the air moves, so a new filter goes in facing the right way.
ah_media_clearance: The open space the filter needs to slide out. Keep it clear.
ah_media_speck_00: Dust, hair and pollen in the air. The filter catches it.

mixing_valve.title: Mixing valve
mixing_valve.typical: a typical anti scald mixing valve on a water heater

heat.say: Water leaves the tank hotter than you want at a tap. The mixing valve on top blends in just enough cold water so what reaches your faucets stays near 120 degrees. A heat sensing part inside moves a small shuttle to keep that balance, even when someone else turns on water.

lessons.label: Why the tank runs hotter
lessons.say: With the valve in place the tank can be kept around 145 degrees. That stores more usable hot water and helps keep germs from growing in the tank, while the valve keeps the taps at a safer 120. The setting is under the cap on top, and a technician checks it with a thermometer at a faucet.

lessons.label: When it wears out
lessons.say: If the heat sensing part wears out or the shuttle sticks, the valve stops mixing and tank hot water can come straight through. If the hot water at your taps suddenly feels hotter than usual, have the valve checked.

lessons.label: Hot water faster
lessons.say: Some homes add a small pump right after the valve. It moves warm water out to the farthest sink, where a small valve lets it come back through the cold pipe to the heater. Hot water then reaches that faucet in seconds, instead of running down the drain while you wait.

lessons.label: The pump timer
lessons.say: The timer runs the pump only at the times you usually want hot water, like mornings and evenings. Push in the tabs for those hours. Running it less saves power and keeps the tank from losing heat all day.

tmv_body: A brass valve that blends hot water from the tank with cold, so the water at your taps stays at a safe temperature.
tmv_cap: Covers the setting. Lifting it lets a technician turn the temperature up or down.
tmv_stem: Turned to set the temperature. A pointer reads against the scale under the cap.
tmv_marks: Show which side takes hot water from the tank, which takes cold, and where the mixed water leaves.
tmv_bonnet: The top piece that holds the parts inside the valve. It comes off when the inside needs service.
tmv_element: Grows and shrinks with the water temperature and moves the shuttle to let in more or less hot water.
tmv_shuttle: A small sliding part between the hot and cold openings. Its position sets how much of each gets through.
tmv_seat_hot: The openings the shuttle slides between. One side lets in hot water, the other cold.
tmv_check_module_hot: Small one way valves on the hot and cold inlets. They stop hot water from pushing into the cold pipe, or cold into the hot.
tmv_filter_washer_hot: Fine screens that catch grit before it can jam the shuttle.
tmv_return_spring: Pushes the shuttle back as the element cools, so the mix stays steady.
tmv_unions: Join the valve to the pipes and let it come out for service without cutting pipe.
element_failed: A heat sensing element that no longer moves. The valve stops mixing and the water can run too hot.
shuttle_stuck: A shuttle jammed against the cold side, for example by scale or grit. Hot water from the tank comes straight through.
hot_line: Carries hot water from the heater's outlet up into the valve.
cold_line: Brings cold water to the valve so it can be blended in.
cold_tee: Splits the house cold line, one way to the heater and one way to the mixing valve.
cold_check: Lets cold water flow to the valve one way only, so hot water cannot push back into the cold pipe.
mixed_line: Tempered water leaves the valve here on its way to the faucets.
mixed_coupling: Where the mixed water line joins the hot water pipe that runs to the house.
tmv_recirc_pump: A small pump that keeps warm water moving out to the farthest faucet, so hot water arrives quickly.
tmv_recirc_timer: A 24 hour dial with push in tabs. The pump runs only during the hours set.
tmv_recirc_pipe: Carries tempered water from the valve, through the pump, to the house.
tmv_recirc_unions: Let the pump come out for service without cutting pipe.
tmv_recirc_board: A board the pump is strapped to, so its weight is not hanging on the pipe.
tmv_recirc_cord: Carries power from the outlet to the pump.
ctx_house_cold: The home's cold line. With a recirculation pump it also carries water back to the heater.
ctx_house_hot_drop: The pipe that carries tempered water to the faucets.

heat.say: Inside the tank a rubber diaphragm keeps water apart from a cushion of air. The well pump fills the tank and squeezes the air, and the pressure rises until the switch turns the pump off. When you open a tap, the air pushes the water out, so the pump does not have to start for every glass of water. Open Cut open to see the inside.

lessons.label: Waterlogged tank
lessons.say: Over time the air cushion can leak away, or the diaphragm can tear. Then the tank fills with water and there is nothing left to push it out. The pump starts and stops every few seconds while water runs, and the gauge needle jumps. That is hard on the pump, so it is worth a call. A technician checks the air at the valve on top, with the tank drained, and sets it a little below the pressure where the pump turns on.

lessons.label: Pressure switch
lessons.say: The pressure switch turns the pump on when the pressure drops to its low setting and off at its high setting, often 40 and 60. The gauge beside it shows where the pressure is. There is live power under the cover, so adjusting it is a job for a technician.

lessons.label: Shutoff and drain
lessons.say: The valve after the tank shuts off water to your home, handy if a pipe leaks. The small drain valve at the bottom empties the tank or gives a water sample for testing.

lessons.label: Power to the pump
lessons.say: The switch on the wall turns off power to the well pump. Turn it off if a pipe is leaking or water is running that will not stop, so the pump does not keep pumping.

tank: Holds a cushion of air above stored water, so the pump does not have to start every time you open a tap.
tank_label: Shows the tank's size and the air pressure it came set to.
tank_air_valve: A tire style valve on top. A technician checks and sets the air charge here with the tank drained.
base_ring: The stand the tank sits on, keeping it off the floor.
tank_tee: The fitting under the tank that gathers the switch, gauge, drain and pipes in one place.
pressure_switch: Turns the well pump on when pressure drops low and off when it reaches the high setting.
switch_cover: Keep it on. The switch under it carries live power.
gauge: Shows the water pressure. It should climb slowly while the pump runs and fall slowly as you use water. A needle that jumps fast often means the tank has lost its air.
check_valve: Lets water from the well in and keeps it from flowing back toward the well.
inlet_stub: The line from the well pump comes in here.
outlet_stub: Water leaves the tank here for the rest of your home.
outlet_union: A fitting that comes apart, so the tank can be changed without cutting the pipe.
ball_valve: Turns off water from the tank to your home.
boiler_drain: A hose valve at the bottom, used to drain the tank or take a water sample.
disconnect: Turns off power to the well pump. Turn it off before any work, or if a pipe is leaking.
nm_cable: Carries power from the wall switch to the pressure switch and on to the pump.
water_tank_body: Water held below the diaphragm, ready for your taps.
tank_air_section: Squeezed air above the diaphragm. It pushes the water out when you open a tap.
tank_diaphragm_section: A rubber sheet that keeps the air and the water apart. If it tears, the air is lost and the tank waterlogs.
tank_waterlogged_half: Water where the air cushion should be. The pump starts and stops far too often.
flow_packets_in: Water from the pump filling the tank.
flow_packets_out: Water on its way to your taps.

heat.say: Cleaned water from the treatment tank runs in through the chlorinator and collects here. When the level lifts the float and tips it past its angle, the pump switches on. It pushes the water out to the sprinkler heads in the yard until the level drops and the float hangs back down, which stops it.

lessons.label: The float
lessons.say: The float hangs on a cord tied to the pump's pipe. It rises with the water and only clicks its switch once it tips past its angle. Here one float does both jobs: tipped up, the pump runs. Hanging down, it stops. A float caught on the pipe or a cord is a common reason a pump will not start or will not stop.

lessons.label: High water and the alarm
lessons.say: If the water keeps rising past the float, the pump is not moving it. Many systems have an alarm that sounds at the house when that happens. If yours goes off, cut back on water right away: hold the laundry, dishwasher and long showers, then call for service. The alarm gives you time, it does not mean anything has overflowed.

lessons.label: Pump service
lessons.say: A union on the pump's pipe lets the whole pump lift out through the riser without digging. A technician checks the intake screen at the bottom for buildup, tests the float and makes sure every splice is sealed and dry.

lessons.label: Keep the lid safe
lessons.say: The lid sits at ground level so the tank can be reached without a shovel. Its screws hold it down so a child cannot lift it. Keep every screw in, mow around it gently, and never drive over it. A cracked lid should be replaced.

tank: A buried plastic tank that holds the cleaned water until there is enough to send out to the yard.
seam: The tank comes in two halves, sealed at this band with a gasket and clips so ground water stays out.
riser: A tube from the tank up to the surface, so the lid sits at ground level and the pump can be reached without digging.
riser_adapter: Joins the riser to the top of the tank with a tight seal.
lid: Screwed down so a child cannot lift it. Keep it clear and never drive over it.
lid_gasket: A seal built into the lid that keeps rain and surface water out of the tank.
lid_bolts: Stainless screws that lock the lid down. Every one should be in and snug.
water: The water from the treatment tank, waiting to be pumped. Its normal level sits around the float.
inlet: Where water from the treatment tank comes in, turned down so it enters gently.
inlet_stub: The pipe from the treatment tank, through the chlorinator, into this tank.
inlet_gasket: A rubber seal where the inlet pipe passes through the tank wall.
chlorinator: A tube in the line that holds chlorine tablets. Water flows past them and is disinfected before it is sprayed on the yard.
chlor_tablets: Slow dissolving tablets made for septic systems. Use septic tablets only, never pool tablets, and keep the tube filled.
pump: Sits on the tank floor and pushes the water out to the sprinkler heads. Its screen sits a little off the bottom so it does not pick up settled solids.
discharge_lower: The pipe from the pump up to the union. It comes out with the pump when it is serviced.
discharge_upper: Carries the water from the union out through the riser wall to the spray line.
discharge_90: Turns the pipe out through the riser wall toward the yard.
union: A joint that unscrews by hand so the pump can be lifted out without cutting pipe.
float_onoff: Rises with the water and switches the pump on when it tips past its angle, then off when it hangs back down.
float_cord: The cord that ties the float to the pump's pipe. Its length sets how far the water rises and falls between pump runs.
cords: Tied neatly up the pipe and looped under the lid, so the pump can come up without undoing any wiring.
uf_cable: A buried cable that brings power out from the house. The breaker and outlet for the pump are at the house.
cord_grip: Where the power cable comes through the riser wall, sealed so water does not follow it in.
entry_sealant: A bead of sealant around the cable where it enters the riser.
splice_hot_to_float_sleeve: Where the power cable joins the pump and float wires. Each joint is crimped and covered with sealed heat shrink to keep moisture out.
label_pump: Each cord is labeled PUMP or FLOAT, so the next person in the riser knows which is which.
spray_line: A buried purple pipe that carries the water from the tank out to the sprinkler heads. Purple means it is not drinking water.
spray_head0: Pops up while the pump runs and spreads the treated water over the lawn, then drops back flush with the ground.

septic_tank.title: Septic tank
septic_tank.typical: a typical concrete septic tank with risers

heat.say: Everything that goes down the drains in the house flows into the tank. Heavy solids sink to the bottom as sludge, and grease and light bits float to the top as scum. Bacteria in the tank slowly break some of the solids down. The tees at each end hold those layers back, so only the clearer water in the middle flows on to the drain field.

lessons.label: The tees
lessons.say: The inlet tee points what comes from the house down into the tank, so it does not stir up the scum. The outlet tee takes water from the middle, below the scum and above the sludge. If a tee breaks or falls off, scum can drift out and clog the drain field, so a pumper checks both tees at every pumping.

lessons.label: Pumping
lessons.say: Bacteria cannot break everything down, so the sludge and scum slowly build up. Here they have grown thick, close to the bottom of the outlet tee. Pumping removes them before they reach the field. Many homes need it every 3 to 5 years, depending on the tank size and how many people live there.

lessons.label: Effluent filter
lessons.say: Some tanks have a filter in the outlet tee. It catches small bits before they leave the tank and helps protect the drain field. Not every tank has one. When there is one, it is usually rinsed off at each pumping, and more often if the drains start to slow.

lessons.label: Caring for it
lessons.say: Only toilet paper and body waste belong in the toilet. Wipes, even ones marked flushable, grease, paper towels and medicines build up in the tank or harm the bacteria. Spread laundry loads through the week, and keep cars and heavy equipment off the tank and the field.

tank: A large buried concrete box that holds the wastewater from the house long enough for solids to settle out. It always stays full of water.
lid_inlet: The lid over the end where wastewater comes in from the house. Keep it screwed down so children and pets stay safe.
lid_outlet: The lid over the end where water leaves for the drain field. Keep it screwed down, and never reach or climb into a tank. The air inside is not safe to breathe.
riser_inlet: A plastic tube that brings the tank opening up to the ground, so the tank can be checked and pumped without digging.
inlet_tee: A pipe fitting inside the tank where water from the house comes in. It points the flow downward so the scum on top is not stirred up.
outlet_tee: A pipe fitting at the far end. It draws water from the middle of the tank, so scum and sludge stay behind.
inlet_stub: The short pipe through the tank wall where the sewer line from the house connects.
outlet_stub: The short pipe through the tank wall where clear water leaves for the drain field.
outlet_seal: A rubber seal where the outlet pipe passes through the wall. It keeps ground water out and wastewater in.
effluent_filter: A slotted filter some tanks have inside the outlet tee. It catches small bits before they reach the field and needs a rinse from time to time.
water: The tank always stays full up to the bottom of the outlet pipe. That is normal. Water standing higher than that means something past the tank is slow.
scum_normal: Grease, oils and light bits that float on top. A pumper measures it to know when the tank needs pumping.
scum_heavy: A scum layer this thick is close to the outlet. It is time to pump before it can drift out to the field.
sludge_normal: Heavy solids that settle on the bottom. Bacteria break some of it down, and the rest is pumped out every few years.
sludge_high: Sludge this deep leaves little room for settling, so solids can wash out to the field. It is time to pump.
sewer_line: The pipe that carries everything from the house drains to the tank. It slopes downhill the whole way.
cleanout: A pipe that comes up to the ground between the house and the tank. A plumber uses it to clear a clog in the sewer line.
cleanout_plug: The screw cap on top of the cleanout. Keep it on tight so rain and dirt stay out.
outlet_line: Carries the settled water from the tank out to the drain field, where the soil finishes cleaning it.

shower.title: Tub and shower valve
shower.typical: a typical tub and shower valve

heat.say: Hot and cold pipes come up inside the wall to the valve. Turning the handle opens the cartridge, which mixes the two to the temperature you pick. The water drops down to the tub spout, or, with the diverter pulled up, climbs the pipe to the shower head.

lessons.label: Tub or shower
lessons.say: With the tub running, pull up the knob on the spout and the water goes up to the shower head instead. If water still pours from the spout while the shower is on, the diverter inside the spout is worn. The fix is usually a new spout, not anything in the wall.

lessons.label: The cartridge
lessons.say: The cartridge inside the valve body does the mixing. A shower that drips, a stiff handle, or water that will not get hot are the usual signs it is wearing out. A clip holds it in place. The water has to be off before it comes out, and a plumber can swap it without opening the wall.

lessons.label: Shutting it off
lessons.say: Many valves have two small built in shutoffs on the valve body, one for hot and one for cold. With the handle and trim plate off, a screwdriver turns them to stop the water to just this shower. If your valve has none, the house main is the way to shut it off.

lessons.label: Tub drain
lessons.say: The lever on the round plate under the spout works a plug hidden inside the overflow pipe, which opens and closes the drain. The plate's openings also catch water before the tub can spill over. A slow tub drain is usually hair caught at the strainer or on the linkage.

handle: Turns the cartridge inside the valve. Further around means hotter water.
escutcheon: Covers the hole in the wall around the valve. Its seal keeps shower spray out of the wall, so a loose or gapped plate is worth fixing.
valve_body: The brass body inside the wall. Hot and cold come in, mixed water goes out to the spout and the shower head. It rarely wears out itself.
cartridge: The part that mixes hot and cold. Most valves today also balance pressure, so a toilet flush elsewhere does not turn the shower suddenly hot or cold. It is the part that usually wears.
retainer_clip: A small clip that holds the cartridge in the valve body.
stop_tube: Fits over the cartridge stem. The limit stop sets how far the handle can turn toward hot, which keeps the water from getting too hot. It can be adjusted.
plaster_ground: A plastic cap that protected the valve while the wall was built. It also shows how deep the valve sits behind the tile.
stop_cold_plug: A built in stop on the valve body. A screwdriver turns it to shut off cold water to this shower only.
stop_hot_plug: A built in stop on the valve body. A screwdriver turns it to shut off hot water to this shower only.
riser_hot: Brings hot water up inside the wall to the valve, from the water heater.
riser_cold: Brings cold water up inside the wall to the valve.
spout_drop: Carries mixed water from the bottom of the valve down to the tub spout.
shower_riser: Carries mixed water from the top of the valve up to the shower arm.
shower_arm: The bent pipe that comes out of the wall and holds the shower head. A small flange covers the hole.
shower_head: Spreads the water into spray. Hard water leaves mineral in the small holes; soaking the head in vinegar often clears weak or crooked spray.
spout: Fills the tub. Many slide onto a pipe and are held by a small screw underneath, others screw on.
diverter_knob: Pull it up to send water to the shower head. It drops back down when the water is turned off.
overflow_plate: The round plate under the spout. It hides the overflow opening and holds the drain lever.
trip_lever: Flip it to open or close the tub drain.
trip_linkage: Hangs inside the overflow pipe and moves the plug when you flip the lever. Hair can wrap around it and slow the drain.
waste_overflow: Joins the tub's bottom drain and its overflow opening into one pipe below the tub.
strainer: The grate in the tub floor. It catches hair, so clearing it now and then keeps water moving.
p_trap: The U shaped bend under the tub. It holds a little water that keeps sewer gas out of the bathroom.
trap_water: The water that always sits in the trap and seals out sewer gas.
drain_line: Carries the tub's water away to the house drain.
tub: The bathtub itself, sitting on the floor framing.
tub_apron: The finished front face of the tub.
valve_wall: The tiled wall the valve sits behind. Keeping its grout and caulk sound keeps water out of the wall.
caulk: The flexible seal where the tub meets the walls. When it cracks or peels, water can get behind the tub, so it is worth redoing.
framing: The wood framing the valve and pipes are fastened to inside the wall.

smart_shutoff.title: Smart water shutoff
smart_shutoff.typical: a typical smart water shutoff in a yard box

heat.say: Water from the meter passes a hand valve and a check valve, then runs through the smart shutoff. A small turbine inside measures the flow and the display counts the gallons.
