If it sees water running in a way that looks like a leak, it can close its own valve and send an alert to your phone.

lessons.label: Shutting off a leak
lessons.say: When a leak sensor gets wet, or the water use looks wrong, a small motor turns the ball inside a quarter turn and the water stops. The light blinks red and the check valve flap falls shut. Once the leak is fixed, the valve can be opened again from the app.

lessons.label: Talking to the hub
lessons.say: The shutoff talks by long range radio to a small hub inside your home, and the hub connects to your internet. A leak sensor near a water heater or washer can signal the shutoff to close, even from across the house.

lessons.label: The hand valve
lessons.say: Just before the smart shutoff sits a plain ball valve with a red handle. A quarter turn shuts the water off by hand, for repairs or if the smart valve cannot be reached. It is good to know where it is.

lessons.label: Sprinklers
lessons.say: In a home with a sprinkler system, the sprinkler line tees off before both valves. That way closing the shutoff never stops the sprinklers, and sprinkler water does not pass through the smart shutoff at all.

box_lid: The lid you see in the lawn. Lift it to read the display or reach the valves.
valve_box: A plastic box set level with the ground. It keeps the valves reachable without digging.
valve_box_gravel: Small gravel under the box so water can drain away from the pipes.
valve_box_knockout: A plugged hole in the box wall. It can be opened if a sprinkler line is added later.
housing: A valve with a flow meter and a radio built in. It watches the water going into your home and can turn it off by itself.
body: The metal body the water flows through. The valve ball and the flow turbine sit inside it.
lid: A small hinged cover over the display and buttons. It keeps dirt off the face.
dial: Shows the gallons counted. You can also see the water use in the phone app.
manual_override: Lets the valve be turned by hand with a hex key if the motor or the battery cannot do it.
set_button: Used when the shutoff is first set up with its hub.
led: Blinks green when the valve opens and red when it closes or warns.
battery_cover: The shutoff runs on batteries, with no wires to the house. The app shows when they are getting low.
battery: Powers the motor, the meter and the radio.
motor: A small motor that turns the valve ball a quarter turn to open or close.
pcb: The brains of the shutoff. It counts the flow, decides when water use looks like a leak and talks to the hub.
valve_ball: A ball with a hole through it. Lined up with the pipe, water flows. Turned a quarter turn, the water stops.
valve_stem: Connects the motor to the valve ball.
meter_turbine: A small wheel that spins as water flows past. Its turns are counted to measure the gallons.
flow_arrow: Shows which way the water must flow. It points toward the house.
coupling_in: A threaded nut and tailpiece that join the shutoff to the pipe on the street side.
coupling_out: A threaded nut and tailpiece that join the shutoff to the pipe on the house side.
adapter_in: Joins the plastic pipe to the threaded end of the shutoff.
adapter_out: Joins the threaded end of the shutoff to the plastic pipe toward the house.
pvc_straight: A short straight run before the shutoff. The water needs it to flow smoothly so the meter reads right.
ball_valve: A plain shutoff valve just before the smart one. It turns the water off by hand.
ball_valve_handle: Turn it a quarter turn to shut the water off. In line with the pipe means open.
check_valve: Lets water flow toward the house only. A rubber flap inside falls shut if water tries to flow back.
check_valve_flap: Swings open with the flow and closes when the flow stops or tries to reverse.
inlet_coupling: Joins the line from the meter to the fittings in the box.
pvc_nipple: A short piece of pipe between the coupling and the hand valve.
irrigation_tee: Splits off water for the sprinkler system before the shutoff valves.
irrigation_line: Carries water to the sprinkler system. It is not shut off by the smart valve.

sump_pump.title: Sump pump
sump_pump.typical: a typical sump pump in its pit

heat.say: Water from around the house drains into the pit. As it rises, a float lifts and turns the pump on. The pump pushes the water up the pipe, through a check valve, and away from the house. When the level drops, the float drops and the pump stops.

lessons.label: Stuck float
lessons.say: If the float hangs up on the pit wall, the cord or debris, the pump never starts and the water keeps rising. The higher alarm float sets off the alarm before the water gets too high. Now and then, check that the float moves freely.

lessons.label: Check valve
lessons.say: The check valve holds the water in the pipe when the pump stops. If it fails, that water falls back into the pit and the pump runs again and again, which wears it out. The sound of water rushing back right after the pump stops is a clue.

lessons.label: The alarm
lessons.say: The alarm float sits above the pump float, so it only rises if the pump falls behind. Most alarms have a test button. Press it now and then to make sure it lights and sounds.

lessons.label: Keep the pit clear
lessons.say: Rags, wipes and other trash in the pit can get pulled into the pump or wrap around the float. Keep the lid on and nothing in the pit but water.

basin: The basin set into the ground where the water collects.
lid: Keeps trash, kids and pets out of the pit. Keep it on and sealed.
pump: Sits at the bottom of the pit and pushes the water out and away from the house.
pump_plate: Shows the pump's size and model, handy when it needs replacing.
float_pump: Rises with the water and turns the pump on, then drops and turns it off.
float_pump_stuck: A float caught on the wall, the cord or debris. The pump cannot start.
float_alarm: Sits higher than the pump float. If the water reaches it, the alarm goes off.
discharge: Carries the water from the pump out and away from the house.
check_valve: Keeps the water in the pipe from falling back into the pit when the pump stops.
check_backflow: With a failed check valve, water runs back into the pit and the pump starts again.
ball_valve: Closes the discharge pipe so the pump or check valve can be changed without a flood of water.
inlet: Where water from around the house drains into the pit.
vent: Lets air in and out of the sealed pit as the water rises and falls.
lift_chain: A handle for lifting the pump out of the pit for service.
cords: Power for the pump and the alarm float. Plug the pump straight into an outlet, not an extension cord.
panel: Watches the alarm float and lights and sounds if the water gets too high.
panel_feed: The power supply to the alarm panel.
alarm_light: Lights up when the water is too high, or when you press the test button.
basin_water: Water collected from around the house, waiting for the float to rise.
basin_water_high: Water rising toward the top of the pit because the pump is not keeping up.
basin_silt: Fine dirt that settles at the bottom of the pit. A lot of it can clog the pump.
rag: Rags and wipes can clog the pump or tangle the float.
flow_packets: Water pushed up the pipe by the pump.

surge_protector.title: Whole house surge protector
surge_protector.typical: a typical whole house surge protector inside a breaker panel

heat.say: Most of the time it just sits there. When a sudden spike of voltage comes in on the power lines, from lightning nearby or the utility switching, the parts inside open a quick path and send the extra to ground. Your lights and appliances see a much smaller bump instead of the full spike.

lessons.label: The status lights
lessons.say: Two green lights on the front show it is working. Both lit means it is protecting the house. Take a look now and then, and after a big storm.

lessons.label: When the lights go out
lessons.say: Each surge it stops wears the parts inside a little, and a very large one can use them up at once. Then the lights go dark. Your power stays on, but the house is no longer protected. It has no parts to repair, so a new one goes in.

lessons.label: Its own breaker
lessons.say: It is wired to its own breaker in the panel, and that breaker has to stay on for it to protect anything. If both lights are out, check that its breaker is on. If it has tripped, call an electrician rather than resetting it again and again.

spd_body: Mounted in the breaker panel and wired to it, so it guards every circuit in the house from voltage spikes.
label: Label
Shows the status lights and reads protected when both are lit. There is nothing inside a homeowner should service.
leds_lit: Both green lights on means it is protecting. If one or both are out, it needs a look.
leds_dark: Dark lights mean protection is used up or the device has lost power.
spd_internals: Small discs inside that pass almost nothing at normal voltage and open up during a spike to send it to ground.
spd_internals_burnt: After a big surge, or many over the years, the parts inside are spent and can no longer protect.
hub: Where its four wires leave the case to reach the breaker and the panel's bars.
feet: Screw it firmly inside the panel.
spd_breaker: A two pole breaker that feeds the surge protector. It must be on for the device to work.
lead_black_a: The black wires connect it to its breaker, one to each side of the house's power.
lead_white: Connects to the panel's neutral bar.
lead_green: Connects to the panel's ground bar. Surges are sent away through this path, so a short, tight connection matters.

water_filter.title: Whole house water filter
water_filter.typical: a typical buried whole house water filter

heat.say: Water from the street comes into the box in the yard and across to the buried filter tank. It flows down through a deep bed of filter media that takes out chlorine and catches fine grit. Then it rises up the center tube, back through the box and on to your home.

lessons.label: Backflushing
lessons.say: Now and then the bed gets a cleaning. The valves in the box are set so water runs the other way, down the center tube and up through the bed. The bed lifts and lets go of the dirt it caught, which flows out the hose bib in the box until the water runs clear.

lessons.label: The bypass
lessons.say: Three valves in the box steer the water. In normal use the red and green valves are open and the blue one is shut. For bypass the blue valve opens first, then the red one shuts, and the green one stays open. Your home still has water, but it skips the filter until the valves are set back.

lessons.label: Worn out media
lessons.say: Over time the media fills with what it has caught, starting at the top of the bed. Backflushing helps, but after some years the media is spent and needs to be replaced. If the chlorine smell comes back, or the water pressure seems lower than it used to be, it is time for a check.

lessons.label: Leaks
lessons.say: Water standing in the box, or a soggy patch in the lawn over the tank, can point to a slow leak at a union or at the seal under the filter head. Rain can collect in a box too, so look again on a dry day. If the water is still there, give us a call.

box_lid: The green lid you see in the lawn. One bolt holds it down. Keep it on so dirt and mulch stay out of the box.
lid_bolt: Holds the lid shut so it stays put when it is stepped on or mowed over.
valve_box: A plastic box set level with the ground. It holds the valves and fittings so they can be reached without digging.
pea_gravel: A bed of small gravel under the box. It lets water drain away instead of standing around the pipes.
manifold: The set of pipes and valves in the box. It sends water through the filter, or around it when needed.
v1_handle: Lets street water into the filter. Open in normal use. It is shut for bypass.
v3_handle: The bypass valve. Shut in normal use. When it is open, water can go around the filter.
v4_handle: Sends water on to your home. Open in normal use and in bypass.
hose_bib: A small faucet in the box. During a backflush the dirty water comes out here.
bib_wheel: Opens the hose bib. Leave it shut except during a backflush.
unions: Fittings that unscrew, so the manifold can come apart for service without cutting pipe. A slow drip here can fill the box with water.
filter_adapters: Brass fittings that join the box's pipes to the flexible lines that run to the filter tank.
pex_jumpers: Two flexible lines. One carries water to the filter head, the other brings filtered water back.
filter_head: The cap on top of the tank. It has an inlet and an outlet port, and seals to the tank with an o-ring.
filter_head_oring: Rubber o-rings that seal the head to the tank and to the center tube. A worn seal can leak.
filter_head_pex_adapter_in: Where water from the box enters the filter head.
filter_head_pex_adapter_out: Where filtered water leaves the head to go back through the box to your home.
tank: A tall tank buried beside the box. It holds the filter media and the water above it.
carbon_media: A deep bed of filter granules. As water passes down through it, chlorine is taken out and fine grit is caught.
carbon_loaded: Media that is full of what it has caught. Once most of the bed looks like this, it is time to replace it.
tank_water: Incoming water fills the space above the bed before it works its way down through the media.
riser_tube: Filtered water rises up this tube from the bottom of the tank to the head.
riser_water: Clean water on its way up the center tube.
diffuser_plate: A slotted plate at the bottom of the tank. Water passes through it, the media stays in the tank.
city_line: The water line from your meter. Street water reaches the filter here.
house_line: The water line that carries filtered water to the house.
grass: Everything below this line is buried. Only the box lid shows in the yard.
box_water: Water standing in the box. After rain this can be normal. If it stays on dry days, there may be a leak.
filter_head_wet: A soggy patch around the filter head can mean its seal is leaking.

well_pump.title: Well pump
well_pump.typical: a typical submersible well pump in a drilled well

heat.say: The pump sits down in the well, under the water. When the pressure switch in your home calls for water, it pushes water up the drop pipe. Near the top, the water turns through the side of the casing at the pitless adapter, below ground, and runs in a buried line to the pressure tank.

lessons.label: Check valve
lessons.say: The check valve above the pump lets water go up but not back down. If it leaks, water drains back into the well between uses. The pressure slowly drops while nobody is using water, and the pump turns on by itself. A technician can confirm it by watching the pressure gauge with every tap off.

lessons.label: The well cap
lessons.say: The cap keeps rain, bugs and small animals out of your water. A cracked seal or a loose cap can let them in. Keep the cap bolted down, the casing standing a little above the ground, and the soil sloping away from it.

lessons.label: Down the well
lessons.say: The pump's wire runs down beside the drop pipe, taped to it every few feet. Each time the pump starts it gives a small twist. The rubber torque arrestor keeps the pump centered so it does not rub the casing.

casing: The pipe that lines the well. It keeps dirt and surface water out of your water.
well_cap: Covers the top of the casing. It lets air in while keeping out rain, bugs and small animals.
well_cap_bolts: Hold the cap down tight so it cannot be knocked off or lifted.
cap_seal: A gasket between the cap and the casing that closes the gap.
well_seal_cracked: A gap that can let bugs and surface water into the well. A new seal or cap fixes it.
cap_conduit: Carries the pump wire out of the cap to the junction box.
jbox: Where the pump wire from down the well joins the wire from your home.
jbox_cover: Keeps water out of the wire connections. Leave it on, there is power inside.
wire_splice: The connection between the pump wire and the house wire, sealed against water.
wire_conduit: Protects the wire from your home where it comes up out of the ground.
wire_stub: The buried wire that carries power out to the well.
pitless_outer: A fitting through the side of the casing, below ground. Water turns here and heads to your home underground, safe from freezing.
pitless_slide: The half that holds the drop pipe. It slides up out of the casing, so the pump can be pulled without digging.
service_stub: The buried pipe that carries water from the well to the pressure tank.
drop_pipe: Carries water up from the pump to the top of the well.
check_valve: Lets water go up and stops it from draining back into the well when the pump stops.
torque_arrestor: A rubber guide that keeps the pump centered in the casing when it starts with a twist.
pump: A long, slim pump and motor that sit under the water down in the well.
pump_plate: Shows the pump's size and voltage, which a technician needs when replacing it.
pump_cable: Carries power down the well to the pump's motor.
cable_tape: Holds the pump wire to the drop pipe every few feet so it cannot tangle or rub.
water_well_column: Groundwater fills the casing up to its resting level. The pump sits well below it.
flow_packets_up: Water pushed up the drop pipe by the pump.
flow_packets_out: Water leaving the well through the pitless adapter.
backflow_packets: With a leaking check valve, water slips back down into the well between uses.

heat.say: Power from the utility comes in at the top and passes through the main breaker. Two metal bars carry it down the middle, and each breaker clips onto them and feeds one circuit in the house. If a circuit draws too much, its breaker shuts it off before the wires can overheat.

lessons.label: A tripped breaker
lessons.say: When a breaker trips, its handle moves away from on, and it often stops in the middle where it is easy to miss. To reset it, push the handle firmly all the way to off, then back to on. If it trips again right away or keeps tripping, leave it off and call a licensed electrician, because something on that circuit needs a look.

lessons.label: GFCI and AFCI breakers
lessons.say: Breakers with a small TEST button add extra protection. A GFCI breaker shuts off when current leaks out where it should not, such as through water or a person, and guards bathrooms, kitchens, garages and outdoor outlets. An AFCI breaker shuts off when it senses sparking in a loose or damaged wire, and guards bedrooms and living areas. Press TEST about once a month: it should trip, then reset it, off and back on.

lessons.label: The main breaker
lessons.say: The large breaker at the top is the main. Switching it off cuts power to every circuit in the house at once, which is good to know in an emergency. The wires coming in above it stay live even with the main off, which is one reason only a licensed electrician works inside the panel.

lessons.label: Label your breakers
lessons.say: The card inside the door lists what each breaker feeds. A clear, up to date list saves time when something goes dead, and matters most in an emergency. If yours is blank or out of date, a helper and a few minutes switching one breaker at a time will tell you what each one runs.

panel_door: The outer door you open to reach the breaker handles and the circuit list.
circuit_directory: Lists what each breaker feeds. Keep it filled in and up to date.
panel_rating_label: Shows the panel's maker, model and amp rating, often 200 amps. An electrician reads it before adding circuits.
deadfront: The metal cover the breaker handles poke through, often called the dead front. It keeps fingers away from live parts, and only a licensed electrician should take it off.
warning_label: A reminder that live parts sit behind the inner cover.
main_breaker: Shuts off every circuit in the house at once. The wires feeding it from above stay live even when it is off.
main_lug_a: Where the utility's incoming wires bolt on above the main breaker. They are always live.
service_entrance_cable: The large cable from the meter that brings the utility's power into the panel. It is always live.
main_neutral_lug: Where the utility's neutral wire lands. It ties into the neutral bars.
hot_bus_bars: Two metal bars down the middle that carry power from the main. Each breaker clips onto them.
bus_insulator: The plastic base that holds the bus bars apart from the metal box.
neutral_bars: The white wires from the circuits land here, giving each circuit its return path.
ground_bar: Bare and green ground wires land here. They give stray current a safe path so a breaker can trip.
grounding_electrode_conductor: A heavy bare copper wire that runs to a ground rod or other grounding point, tying the system to the earth.
bonding_screw: Ties the neutral to the metal box. It belongs in the main panel only, something an electrician checks.
panel_can: The metal box set in the wall that holds everything. The circuit cables enter through its top.
romex_lights_1_jacket: Each cable feeds one circuit. Black carries power, white is the neutral, bare copper is the ground, and a red wire joins in on 240 volt circuits.
romex_wh_white_tape: On a 240 volt circuit with no neutral, the white wire carries power, so it is marked with tape to say so.
breaker_lights_1: Feeds one circuit and shuts it off if it draws too much. A tripped one often rests in the middle: push it to off, then on.
breaker_bath: A breaker with a TEST button. It also trips on current leaking out (GFCI) or on sparking in a wire (AFCI). Press TEST once a month, then reset it.
breaker_wh: A double wide breaker for a 240 volt appliance like the water heater, the outdoor unit or the air handler. Both halves turn off together.

expansion_tank.title: Expansion tank
expansion_tank.typical: a typical thermal expansion tank on a water heater

heat.say: When the heater warms the water, the water grows a little, around half a gallon in a typical 50 gallon tank. That extra water is pushed back up the cold line and into the expansion tank. Inside, it presses on a rubber diaphragm and squeezes a cushion of air, so the pressure in the pipes stays steady. When you use hot water, the air pushes it back out.

lessons.label: Why it is needed
lessons.say: Many homes have a check valve, a backflow preventer or a pressure reducing valve where the water comes in. These keep water from flowing back toward the street, which also means the extra water from heating has nowhere to go. Without an expansion tank, the pressure in the pipes climbs every time the heater runs. That strains faucets, toilet fill valves and the heater itself, and can make the relief valve drip.

lessons.label: The air charge
lessons.say: The air side comes filled from the factory, often to about 40 psi. To work well, the air charge should match the water pressure in the home. A technician checks it with a tire gauge at the air valve, with the water pressure taken off the tank, and adds or lets out air as needed.

lessons.label: Waterlogged tank
lessons.say: Over the years the air can slowly leak out, or the diaphragm can tear. Then the tank fills with water and can no longer take up the extra, so the pressure jumps each time the heater runs. A common sign is the relief valve on the heater dripping. A simple check is to tap the tank: the air side should sound hollow, while a waterlogged tank sounds dull all over and feels heavy.

lessons.label: What a technician checks
lessons.say: A technician checks the home's water pressure first, then the tank's air charge. A quick press on the air valve tells a lot: air should come out, and water means the diaphragm has failed and the tank needs replacing. They also make sure the tank is well supported, since a tank full of water is heavy, and look for rust or drips at the connection. Many tanks last about 5 to 10 years.

exp_tank_shell_front: A small steel tank on the cold line. It gives the water room to grow as it heats, so the pressure in the pipes stays steady.
exp_tank_water_chamber: The part of the tank open to the cold line. Extra water from heating flows in here, and back out when hot water is used.
exp_tank_diaphragm: A rubber sheet that keeps the water and the air apart. If it tears, the air is lost and the tank waterlogs.
exp_tank_air_chamber: Air sealed in at the factory. It squeezes as extra water comes in and pushes it back out later, like a spring.
exp_tank_air_valve: A tire style valve on the end of the tank. A technician checks and sets the air charge here. Water coming out of it means the diaphragm has failed.
exp_tank_label: Shows the tank's size, its highest safe pressure and the air charge it came set to.
exp_tank_piping: A short pipe that tees the tank into the cold water line, so expanding water can reach it.
exp_tank_strap: Holds the tank steady. Full of water a tank is heavy, so it is best not to let it hang on the pipe alone.
exp_tank_waterlogged: Water where the air cushion should be. The tank can no longer take up the extra water, so the pressure jumps when the heater runs.
take_up_slug_0: Extra water pushed out of the heater as it warms. It flows back up the cold line and into the expansion tank.
waterlogged_spike_0: When the pressure gets too high, the relief valve lets a little water out through its drain pipe. A drip here can mean the expansion tank has lost its air.
cold_supply_line: Brings cold water from the home's supply into the heater. The expansion tank tees into this line.
hot_supply_line: Carries hot water from the heater to the sinks, showers and appliances.
cold_water_inlet: Where cold water enters the heater. As the water heats and grows, some of it backs up out of here toward the expansion tank.
dip_tube: A plastic tube that carries new cold water down to the bottom of the tank, so it does not mix with the hot water on top.
tp_relief_valve: Opens by itself if the tank gets too hot or the pressure too high. If it drips after the heater runs, the expansion tank is one of the first things to check.
tp_discharge_connection: Carries water from the relief valve down toward the floor or a drain, so it cannot spray on anyone.
water_volume: Usually 40 or 50 gallons. As it heats it takes up a little more room, and that extra has to go somewhere.
inner_tank: The heater's tank. Pressure that swings up every time the water heats is hard on it over the years, and the expansion tank helps keep that in check.
outer_jacket: The heater the expansion tank serves. Warming the water is what makes it expand in the first place.
gas_control_valve: The knob on the front. It sets the water temperature and turns the burner on when the tank cools down.
burner: Gas burns here, under the tank, like a stove burner turned upside down.
drain_valve: Used to flush sediment out of the bottom of the tank.

outdoor_faucet.title: Outdoor faucet
outdoor_faucet.typical: a typical outdoor faucet with a freeze cover and a vacuum breaker

heat.say: Water left in an outdoor faucet can freeze in a hard cold snap, swell and split the pipe. A foam cover pressed tight to the wall keeps the cold wind off and holds in a little warmth that travels out along the pipe from the house. Unhook the hose before a freeze, then put the cover on.

lessons.label: The vacuum breaker
lessons.say: The small fitting on the faucet is a vacuum breaker. If the water pressure drops while a hose lies in a bucket, a pool or a sprayer, that water could be pulled back into your pipes. Inside, a spring shuts a rubber disc and lets air in, so the hose drains out its end instead of back into the house.

lessons.label: Draining it for winter
lessons.say: Before a freeze, take the hose off and let the vacuum breaker drain. The black ring at the bottom moves to let the last of the water run out, so nothing is left inside to freeze. Then the cover can go on.

lessons.label: A dripping breaker
lessons.say: A short spurt from the vent when you turn the water on or off is normal. Water that keeps spitting out while the hose runs usually means the rubber disc or seal inside is worn. A technician can repair or replace it.

lessons.label: A loose cover
lessons.say: The cover only works when its foam edge sits flat against the wall. If the cord slips, the cover tips and cold air gets in through the gap. Pull the cord snug on its hook so the cover is pressed tight to the wall again.

ctx_bib: Brings water from the house out to the yard. Its handle turns the water on and off.
ctx_block: A flat block on the wall that the faucet is fastened to. It gives the cover a smooth place to seal.
ctx_wall: The outside wall the faucet comes through. The water pipe runs inside it.
cover_shell: A hard dome that goes over the faucet for the winter. It keeps the cold wind off the faucet.
cover_foam: Foam inside the dome that helps hold in the little bit of warmth coming from the house.
cover_gasket: The soft edge that presses against the wall so cold air cannot sneak in around the cover.
cover_loop: Goes around the faucet behind the handle. Pulling it tight draws the cover against the wall.
cover_hook: Holds the cord tight at the end of the cover so the cover stays pressed to the wall.
cover_gasket_gap: This cover has slipped and cold air gets in through the gap. Pull the cord snug again.
cover_cutaway: The cover cut in half, to show the foam and the faucet inside.
warm_band: A little heat travels out along the pipe from inside the house. The cover keeps it around the faucet.
cold_packet_00: Freezing air outside. The cover keeps it from reaching the faucet.
vb_adapter: Screws onto the faucet's hose thread. It stops hose water from being pulled back into your pipes.
vb_lower_body: The brass body that holds the working parts. Your hose screws onto its bottom.
vb_gasket_washer: Seals the vacuum breaker to the faucet so it does not leak at the top.
vb_cap: The black ring at the bottom. It covers the air vents and lets the breaker drain for winter.
vb_check_disc: Opens when water flows out to the hose and shuts when the pressure drops, so water cannot flow back.
vb_spring: Pushes the disc shut the moment the water pressure falls.
vb_set_screw: Its head snaps off when the breaker is put on, so the breaker cannot be unscrewed by mistake.
vb_hose_thread: Where your garden hose screws on.
vb_vent_drip: Water spitting from the vent while the hose runs. It usually means the disc or seal inside is worn.
vb_story_bucket: A hose left in a bucket, pool or sprayer is how dirty water can get pulled back. The breaker stops it.
vb_story_hose_tube: When the pressure drops, the water in the hose drains out its end instead of back into the house.
vb_air_in_0: When the pressure drops, the breaker lets air in through its vents instead of pulling water back.
vb_hose_packets: The hose empties out its far end, away from your pipes.

heat.say: A package unit keeps the cooling and the heating in one cabinet outside, with ducts running through the wall to your rooms. In summer, the compressor and the outdoor coil carry heat out of your home while the blower pushes house air across a cold indoor coil. In winter, gas burners heat a metal heat exchanger and the blower carries that warmth into the ducts.

lessons.label: The air filter
lessons.say: House air comes back through the return duct and passes through a filter before it is heated or cooled. In this unit the filter sits behind a panel on the side. A clogged filter starves the unit of air, so check it every month or two and change it when it looks gray. Some homes have the filter at a grille inside the house instead.

lessons.label: Keep the coil clear
lessons.say: The outdoor coil sits behind the grille at the corner of the unit. Air has to pass through it freely to carry the heat away. Keep plants, grass clippings and leaves about two feet away, and keep the top clear for the fan. A dirty coil makes the unit work harder and cool less.

lessons.label: The gas heat
lessons.say: When the heat comes on, a small fan called the inducer starts first to clear the vent. Then a spark lights the gas at the burners, and the flames heat the inside of the heat exchanger. House air passes over the outside of it, so the exhaust never mixes with the air you breathe. A yearly check looks for rust, soot and cracks.

lessons.label: The condensate drain
lessons.say: In summer the indoor coil pulls water out of the air. It drips into a pan and leaves through a small pipe with a trap at the front of the unit. If the line clogs with algae or dirt, water can back up and pool around the pad. Keep the end of the line open and clear.

cabinet: The metal case that holds the whole system, cooling and gas heat together, outside the house.
coil_grille: The louvered panels in front of the outdoor coil. They protect the coil and let air pass through.
fan_grille: The grille on top. The outdoor fan blows the heat out through here, so keep it clear.
filter_panel_cover: The side panel the filter slides in behind. It comes off for a filter change.
blower_panel_cover: Covers the blower that moves air through your ducts. A technician opens it for service.
burner_panel_cover: Covers the gas burners and the controls for the heat. A job for a technician.
compressor_panel_cover: Covers the compressor and its electrical parts. Only a technician should open it.
control_panel_cover: Covers the control board and wiring that run the unit.
data_plate: Data label
Lists the model, size and age of the unit. Handy to have when you call for service.
hoods: Let in air for the burners and let the exhaust out. Keep them clear of plants and nests.
burner_assembly: Where the gas burns when the heat is on.
flames: The burning gas. They heat the inside of the heat exchanger.
gas_valve: Opens to send gas to the burners when the heat is called for, and shuts it off when it is not.
igniter: Makes a spark that lights the gas.
heat_exchanger: Metal tubes the flames heat from the inside. House air passes over the outside and warms up.
inducer: A small fan that pulls the exhaust through the heat exchanger and pushes it out the vent hood.
pressure_switch: A safety switch that checks the inducer is moving the exhaust before the gas can come on.
limit_switches: Shut the burners off if the unit gets too hot, for example from a clogged filter.
blower_housing: The curved case around the blower wheel that aims the air into the supply duct.
blower_wheel: Spins to move house air across the coil or heat exchanger and out to your rooms.
evap_coil: Gets cold in summer and cools the house air passing through it. It also pulls water out of the air.
filter: Catches dust before the air is heated or cooled. Check it every month or two.
filter_rack: Holds the filter in place in the return air path.
control_board: The unit's brain. It follows the thermostat and starts each part in the right order.
compressor: The heart of the cooling. It pumps the refrigerant and squeezes it so it can give off its heat outside.
outdoor_coil: Thin metal fins around copper tubing. The heat from your home leaves through here. Keep it clean and clear.
fan: Pulls outdoor air through the coil and blows the heat out the top.
condensate_stub: Carries water from the indoor coil's pan out the front of the unit.
condensate_drain: The small pipe and trap that lead the water away from the unit. Keep its end open.
condensate_pool: Water pooling here can mean the drain line is clogged.
gas_pipe: Brings gas to the unit. It has a shutoff valve near the unit.
drip_leg: A short capped pipe on the gas line that catches dirt and moisture before they reach the gas valve.
disconnect: The box on the wall near the unit. It cuts the power to the unit for service.
duct_connection: Carry air between the unit and the house, through the wall. One brings air back, one sends it out.
pad: The unit sits on a level pad that keeps it off the dirt and lets water drain away. A pad that sinks or tilts can strain the pipes and the drain.

heat.say: Most of the time it simply passes power to whatever is plugged in. When a sudden spike comes down the wires, small parts inside called MOVs open a quick path and send the extra toward the ground wire. What is plugged in sees a much smaller bump instead of the full spike.

lessons.label: When protection runs out
lessons.say: Each surge wears the protection parts a little, and a big one can use them up at once. A small fuse inside then opens, the light on the face goes dark and an alarm beeps. Depending on the model, the outlet may keep giving power with no protection, or shut off. It has no parts to repair, so a new one goes in.

lessons.label: Silencing the alarm
lessons.say: A small recessed control on the face turns the beeping off. Silencing it does not bring the protection back. It only stops the noise until the outlet is replaced.

lessons.label: Behind the plate
lessons.say: In the wall box, the black, white and bare copper wires land on screws on the sides. The ground wire matters most here, since it is the path the surge is sent down. Replacing an outlet is work for a licensed electrician, with the breaker off.

face: Where you plug in. It also carries the protected light and the alarm mute.
led_lit: Lit means the surge protection is working.
led_dark: A dark light means the protection is used up, or the outlet has no power.
mute_screw: Turns off the beeping once protection is lost. It does not restore protection.
buzzer: Beeps when the protection parts are used up, so you know to replace the outlet.
mov_1: Small discs called MOVs. They pass almost nothing at normal voltage and open up during a spike to steer it away.
mov_1_burnt: After a big surge, or many over the years, this part is worn out and can no longer protect.
thermal_fuse: Opens if the surge parts overheat as they wear out, which takes them out of the circuit safely.
thermal_fuse_blown: The fuse has opened, so the protection is gone and the alarm and dark light say so.
pcb: Holds the surge parts, the light and the alarm, and links them to the outlet's contacts.
surge_bolt: A brief spike of extra voltage, from lightning nearby or the power company switching lines.
contact_line: Brass strips behind the narrower slots. They carry the power.
contact_neutral: Strips behind the wider slots. They carry the current back.
contact_ground: Behind the round hole. They connect a plug's ground pin to the ground wire.
screw_line_top: Where the black hot wire lands.
screw_neutral_top: Where the white neutral wire lands.
screw_ground: Where the bare copper ground wire lands.
strap: The metal frame that screws the outlet to the wall box.
base: The plastic body that holds the contacts and the surge parts.
back_cover: Closes the back of the outlet over the surge parts.
strip_gauge: A mark that shows how much insulation to strip off a wire before it is connected.
plate: The cover around the outlet. It keeps fingers away from the wiring behind it.
gang_box: The box in the wall that holds the outlet and its wire connections.
nm_cable: The cable that brings power from the breaker panel to this outlet.
wire_black: The hot wire that brings power.
wire_white: The neutral, which carries current back to the panel.
wire_bare: Bare copper. It gives a surge, or a fault, a safe path away.
stud: The wood framing the wall box is nailed to.

heat.say: It measures the room's temperature and compares it to the number you set. When the room drifts too far, it closes a switch on a small low voltage wire to call for heating or cooling, and the system starts. When the room reaches your setting, it lets go and the system stops.

lessons.label: Batteries
lessons.say: This kind keeps its settings and screen running on two AA batteries tucked in the back of the face. If the screen fades or goes blank, pull the face gently straight off the wall plate, put in fresh batteries and press it back on. Many people simply change them once a year.

lessons.label: The wires
lessons.say: Behind the face, thin colored wires run to the furnace or air handler. Red brings low voltage power, white calls for heat, yellow for cooling and green for the fan. The blue one here is the C wire, the common, which gives the thermostat steady power. Colors are a habit rather than a rule, so a technician goes by the letters on the plate.

lessons.label: Settings
lessons.say: Mode picks heat, cool or off. Fan on Auto runs the blower only while heating or cooling, and On runs it all the time. A schedule that sets back a few degrees while you sleep or are away saves energy without giving up comfort.

head_shell: The part you see on the wall. It holds the screen, buttons, batteries and temperature sensor, and it unplugs from the wall plate.
head_lcd: Shows the room temperature, your setting, the mode and the fan.
head_digit_now_0_a: The large numbers show the temperature the thermostat reads right now.
head_digit_set_0_a: The number you have asked for. The system runs until the room reaches it.
head_ctl_up: Raise or lower the set temperature.
head_ctl_mode: Switches between heat, cool and off.
head_ctl_fan: Auto runs the blower only with heating or cooling. On runs it all the time.
head_ctl_menu: Opens the clock and schedule settings.
battery_aa_1: Two AA batteries keep it running. Fresh ones once a year is a good habit.
head_battery_tray: Holds the batteries in the back of the face, reached by pulling the face off the wall plate.
head_contacts: Meet the pins on the wall plate when the face is pressed on, so no wires go to the face itself.
sub_plate: Screwed to the wall. The wires land on it, and the face clips on in front.
sub_pins: Carry the signals from the wall plate's terminals to the face.
sub_term_r: Each wire lands under a lettered terminal: R power, C common, W heat, Y cooling, G fan, and others for heat pumps and extra stages.
sub_slider_r_rc: Joins the two power terminals when one transformer runs both heating and cooling.
cable_red: Usually R, the 24 volt power from the system's transformer.
cable_white: Usually W, which calls for heat.
cable_green: Usually G, which turns on the blower fan.
cable_yellow: Usually Y, which calls for cooling.
cable_blue: Here it is the C wire, the common, which completes the circuit so the thermostat has steady power.
cable_jacket: The thin cable inside the wall that carries the wires to the furnace or air handler. It is low voltage.
sub_mount_screw_1: Hold the wall plate to the wall.
sub_wall_anchor_1: Plastic anchors that give the screws a firm grip in drywall.

washer_box.title: Washer valve box
washer_box.typical: a typical washing machine valve box

heat.say: Two valves in the wall feed hot and cold water to the washer through its hoses. The washer snaps its own water valves shut many times a load, and the moving water slams to a stop. That knock is called water hammer. The small arrestors beside the valves hold a cushion of air behind a piston that soaks up the shock.

lessons.label: Turning the water off
lessons.say: Turning both handles off stops the water to the washer. It is a good habit when you leave home for a few days, and the first thing to do if a hose starts to leak. If a valve is stiff or drips at the handle, have it looked at before it fails.

lessons.label: Washer hoses
lessons.say: The washer's hoses screw onto these valves and stay under full water pressure all the time, even when the washer is off. A hose that bursts can put a lot of water on the floor fast. Check them for bulges, cracks or rust at the ends, and replace them about every five years. Braided steel hoses hold up better than plain rubber.

lessons.label: The drain
lessons.say: The washer's drain hose hooks into this opening and empties into the drain pipe below. Keep the hose pushed in and held so it cannot pop out when the washer pumps. If water backs up here, the drain line may be clogged with lint.

box_shell: A plastic box set into the wall that keeps the washer's valves and drain neatly in one place.
valve_hot: The washer's hot water hose screws on here. Its handle shuts off the hot water.
valve_cold: The washer's cold water hose screws on here. Its handle shuts off the cold water.
handle_hot: Turn it to shut off the hot water to the washer.
handle_cold: Turn it to shut off the cold water to the washer.
supply_hot_pushfit: The pipe in the wall that brings hot water up to the valve.
supply_cold_pushfit: The pipe in the wall that brings cold water up to the valve.
hammer_arrestor_hot: A small capped chamber that soaks up the knock when the washer shuts its water off fast.
hammer_arrestor_cold: A small capped chamber on the cold side that soaks up the knock when the water stops fast.
hammer_air_cushion: Trapped air that squeezes like a spring when the water slams to a stop.
hammer_piston: Keeps the water and the air apart. It slides up when a surge hits, then settles back.
hammer_water: When the flow stops suddenly, water pushes into the arrestor instead of banging the pipes.
drain_bore: The washer's drain hose hooks in here and empties into the drain pipe.
drain_collar: Joins the box to the drain pipe in the wall.
